📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (906 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Iamnaples

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that chiude con un bilancio utile la SSC Napoli dopo la perdita registrata nell’esercizio precedente.
  • Sources indicate that stando ai documenti ufficiali, il Napoli ha archiviato l’esercizio al 30 giugno 2026 con un valore della produzione di 384,3 milioni di euro, rispetto ai circa 291 milioni dell’annata precedente.
  • Nell’esercizio chiuso al 30 giugno 2022, il Napoli aveva contabilizzato 12,1 milioni di euro di ricavi da gara e ulteriori 37,2 milioni provenienti da sponsorizzazioni, attività commerciali e royalties, per un totale di 49,3 milioni.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that chiude con un bilancio utile la SSC Napoli dopo la perdita registrata nell’esercizio precedente. Il ritorno in Champions League, il peso delle operazioni di mercato, il risarcimento ottenuto nell’ambito del contenzioso con IMG e lo sviluppo del comparto commerciale hanno permesso alla società partenopea di migliorare i propri risultati economici, a fronte di una crescita altrettanto significativa dei costi.

Sources indicate that stando ai documenti ufficiali, il Napoli ha archiviato l’esercizio al 30 giugno 2026 con un valore della produzione di 384,3 milioni di euro, rispetto ai circa 291 milioni dell’annata precedente. E’ un primato assoluto nella storia della società di Aurelio De Laurentiis, che supera anche i 359,2 milioni contabilizzati nel 2022/2023, stagione culminata con la conquista del terzo scudetto. Le entrate derivanti dai diritti televisivi hanno raggiunto quota 133 milioni di euro, contro i 78,1 milioni della stagione 2024/2025. Nello specifico, gli introiti provenienti dalle competizioni UEFA sono cresciuti da 3,9 a 49,5 milioni di euro, ai quali si aggiungono quelli legati alla partecipazione alla Supercoppa italiana. Le plusvalenze derivanti dalle cessioni dei calciatori si sono attestate intorno ai 102,7 milioni di euro. L’operazione più remunerativa è stata quella riguardante Victor Osimhen, che ha assicurato al club una plusvalenza di circa 73,2 milioni di euro. Tra le altre cessioni più significative ci sono quelle di Giacomo Raspadori, Alessandro Zanoli e Giovanni Simeone. I trasferimenti a titolo temporaneo hanno inoltre generato proventi per circa 8,7 milioni di euro. Nel dettaglio, ecco come si compongono i ricavi della SSC Napoli: Ricavi da gare: 31,3 milioni di euro (24,1 milioni nel 2024/2025); Ricavi da sponsorizzazioni: 52,9 milioni (48,1 milioni); Ricavi commerciali e royalties: 25,5 milioni (20,1 milioni); Proventi vari: 1,7 milioni (1,3 milioni); Proventi da cessione dei diritti televisivi: 133 milioni (78,1 milioni); Plusvalenze da cessione dei calciatori: 102,7 milioni (102,6 milioni); Altri ricavi e proventi diversi: 36,8 milioni (16,6 milioni); Contributi in conto esercizio: 500mila euro (0 euro); Totale: 384,3 milioni (290,9 milioni). Nella voce relativa agli altri proventi rientra anche un’entrata straordinaria derivante dall’accordo transattivo raggiunto dalla Lega Serie A nell’ambito della controversia con IMG per i diritti audiovisivi internazionali. L’intesa ha garantito alla società azzurra un introito di 19,3 milioni di euro.

Nell’esercizio chiuso al 30 giugno 2022, il Napoli aveva contabilizzato 12,1 milioni di euro di ricavi da gara e ulteriori 37,2 milioni provenienti da sponsorizzazioni, attività commerciali e royalties, per un totale di 49,3 milioni. Nella stagione 2025/2026, queste stesse voci hanno raggiunto complessivamente 109,7 milioni di euro, di cui: 31,3 milioni derivanti dal matchday, 52,9 milioni dalle sponsorizzazioni e 25,5 milioni dalle attività commerciali e dalle royalties.

Aumentano anche i costi di gestione. I costi della produzione hanno raggiunto quota 373,3 milioni di euro, rispetto ai 315,5 milioni dell’esercizio precedente, con una crescita di circa il 18%. Di seguito il dettaglio delle principali voci di costo del bilancio azzurro:.

-Materie prime, sussidiarie, di consumo e merci: 10,4 milioni di euro (6,5 milioni nel 2024/2025);.

-Costi per servizi: 30,5 milioni (36 milioni); Costi per godimento di beni di terzi: 8,1 milioni (6,7 milioni);.

-Costi per il personale: 172,3 milioni (142,1 milioni), di cui 165,3 milioni per salari e stipendi (135,8 milioni);.

-Ammortamenti e svalutazioni: 135 milioni (118,2 milioni);.

-Variazione delle rimanenze: -800mila euro (-100mila euro);.

-Oneri diversi di gestione: 17,7 milioni (6,2 milioni); Totale: 373,3 milioni (315,5 milioni).

A incidere maggiormente sull’aumento delle spese è stato il costo della squadra, anche in delle virtù operazioni sul mercato effettuate per soddisfare le richieste dell’ex allenatore Antonio Conte. Infatti, la voce salari è cresciuta dai 132,9 milioni dell’esercizio precedente ai 161,9 milioni contabilizzati al 30 giugno 2026. I soli compensi contrattuali dei calciatori hanno raggiunto quota 128,9 milioni di euro, ai quali si aggiungono i premi legati al conseguimento dei risultati sportivi, anch’essi in aumento.

It has been revealed that tuttavia, la crescita del fatturato ha permesso al Napoli di tornare a registrare un risultato economico positivo. La differenza tra il valore ei costi della produzione si è attestata intorno agli 11 milioni di euro, invertendo la tendenza negativa dell’esercizio precedente. Al netto della componente fiscale, il Napoli ha archiviato il bilancio al 30 giugno 2026 con un utile di circa 2,2 milioni di euro. Un risultato in netto miglioramento rispetto alla perdita di 21,4 milioni di euro registrata dodici mesi prima. Il club partenopeo torna quindi in utile dopo un solo anno caratterizzato da un risultato economico negativo, raggiungendo contestualmente il fatturato più elevato della propria storia.

Industry observers note that infine, sul documento contabile ci sono indicazioni significative anche sulla situazione patrimoniale e finanziaria della SSC Napoli. Il patrimonio netto si mantiene ampiamente positivo, attestandosi a circa 192,4 milioni di euro, mentre le disponibilità liquide ammontano a 172,9 milioni.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jamal Musiala is set to return to Bayern Munich’s matchday squad for Friday’s Bundesliga clash against Cologne, according to Sport1.

The 23-year-old has been sidelined since suffering a torn muscle fibre during a warm-up prior to Germany’s UEFA Nations League game against the Netherlands on 24 September.

Musiala has featured just three times in the Bundesliga for Germany’s record champions this season, returning a goal and assist, while also scoring in his only UEFA Champions League game in 2026/27.

It goes without saying that this is providing that Musiala, who has been training for the last 10 days, doesn’t suffer any setbacks in training during the week.

Sources indicate that bayern could, however, be without Alphonso Davies. The 25-year-old sustained an injury while on international duty with Canada, lasting just six minutes of his nation’s 3-2 CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final win over Guatemala after picking up an injury on 13 November.

Speaking to Canada’s One Soccer, Davies remarked: “At the beginning of the game everything seemed good. I fell down. They’re analysing the footage. I think my back twisted when I slipped. I tried to get up as promptly as possible to block the shot. As soon as I raised my leg and put it down to block the shot, I felt something […] Hopefully it’s not too bad.”.

Industry News: 'I was one day away from falling into a coma': JAKE O'BRIEN, the Premier League's only diabetic player, on his brush with death, managing his condition in the dressing room - and why he was 'never close' to leaving Everton last summer

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1586 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 21:00 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 08:25 EST, 13 November 2026.
  • According to recent reports, there are few sights more incendiary to the modern manager than a footballer reaching for his phone as soon as he walks through the dressing room door.
  • But the Everton and Republic of Ireland defender had a good excuse: he’s the only Type One diabetic playing in the Premier League.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 21:00 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 08:25 EST, 13 November 2026.

According to recent reports, there are few sights more incendiary to the modern manager than a footballer reaching for his phone as soon as he walks through the dressing room door. So you can imagine the reaction Jake O’Brien received when he pulled out his mobile just before one half-time team talk.

But the Everton and Republic of Ireland defender had a good excuse: he’s the only Type One diabetic playing in the Premier League.

O’Brien’s body is unable to create insulin, the hormone that regulates the amount of glucose in your blood.

In a recent development, loaded on his mobile is an app linked via Bluetooth to a circular device on his arm which gives a reading of his blood sugar levels. It is then that he takes out a needle and injects the necessary insulin dose into his thigh or stomach.

It has been revealed that ‘There was one guy who didn’t react too well. Mentioning no names! He was saying: "What are you doing on your phone?"' O’Brien recalls. ‘But he soon realised what it was for.’.

It can also come as a shock to the uninitiated among his team-mates.

‘One or two are taken aback at first,’ he claims. ‘It can be a bit confusing. “What’s he doing?’’ Or maybe those that are a little squeamish, but they soon get used to it. It's only a small needle.'.

Everton and Ireland defender Jake O'Brien is the only diabetic footballer in the Premier League.

O'Brien (pictured attending an awareness workshop put on by Everton) revels in the role of being a diabetes ambassador.

O'Brien (pictured with his partner Sophie) indicates some of his team-mates are 'taken aback' when he injects himself with insulin (Source: Instagram/Obrienjake_).

Tracking blood glucose levels is now an everyday part of O'Brien's life but it is a life that was unwittingly put in jeopardy prior to his diagnosis at 16.

O’Brien was later told he had been just one day away from slipping into a coma when his concerned parents ushered him to the doctors near the family home in Youghal, County Cork, for a check-up.

In a recent development, their sports-mad son, who had won national titles at boxing and hurling, was tired, losing weight and had an insatiable thirst despite drinking eight to nine litres of water a day. He had lost seven kilograms in just over a week. A blood test revealed his blood sugar was ten times what was considered stable and he was rushed to hospital.

Sources indicate that ‘I was told I was a day away from a coma,' notes O'Brien. 'If I had gone to sleep that night without having gone to the doctor, who knows?’.

It has been revealed that he went into hospital that night weighing 53kg, or just over eight stone. Two weeks post-diagnosis he was back up to 60kg, and within two years he had put on a whopping 30kg.

According to recent reports, 'Yeah, 30kg,' laughs O'Brien. 'I know it's not normal. It must have been some grocery bill for Mum, but I was motivated to put on the weight, going to the gym all the time.

According to recent reports, ‘I was a bit naive about it all,' he deadpans. ‘I never expected to have anything but once I knew what diabetes was, I didn’t wallow in it, I took it as a positive. Everything just clicked for me physically. I just thought, "Right, now I know what’s wrong, I can get on with my life again".

‘It was a pain going in and out of hospital, but I just took it as education and wanted to get my sport back on track.

'My family are... I wouldn't say cold, but matter of fact. Supportive, obviously, but they are all sporty too, so it was just, "Get on with it".'.

O'Brien's life in the Premier League would have seemed inconceivable when he fell down to 53kg as a teenager and was hospitalised.

Recent findings suggest that he is now an imposing 6ft 6in tall, weighing around 96kg. His physique offers no outward indication of the daily challenge he is dealing with.

Sources indicate that today, relaxing in the cafe at Everton’s Finch Farm training complex, O’Brien is an imposing 6ft 6in tall, weighing around 96kg. His physique offers no outward indication of the daily challenge he is dealing with.

There’s a Cork-lilt to his softly spoken Irish tone. He’s polite and engaging and it’s clear he revels in the role of being a diabetes ambassador, spreading the message that diagnosis doesn’t have to end your dreams.

Such has been his impact, he has even attracted support from fans of the other club in the city.

One, six-year-old Liverpool fan Louis, reached out via Instagram to ask O’Brien how he kept up his glucose levels during a game and whether he suffered any ‘hypos’ - the expression for hypoglycemic episodes, when the blood sugar drops too low and leaves you faint or dizzy.

Recent findings suggest that louis, whose siblings Paisley and Evie also have Type One diabetes, followed up by challenging O’Brien to a penalty shootout. If the Everton man lost, he faced a forfeit, he would have to shout ‘Up the Reds’ on social media.

‘You play for the wrong team but you're still a Type One hero, and Mum states you're proof that diabetes doesn't stop you from playing at the top level,’ posted Louis.

Touched by the message, O’Brien asked Everton to invite the youngster and his family to training for a kickabout, although ultimately, we are assured they reached a compromise on the penalties forfeit.

‘I’ve struck up a rapport with some kids and groups here and in Ireland,' indicates O'Brien. 'They often have the same story as mine of not being sure what the future holds.

‘There’s a big misconception about diabetes over what it is and the limitations it brings.

‘Just because you have diabetes doesn’t mean your dreams are over.’.

‘Adrenaline is higher on match days so that can change how you feel. I may inject four times before a night game and a bit more at half-time'.

‘Just because you have diabetes doesn’t mean your dreams are over,’ notes O'Brien, who also excelled at boxing and hurling as a boy (Source: TikTok/Everton).

The centre back credits boxing for helping discipline with his diet but underlines ‘no food is off limits, it’s just about applying common sense'.

In a recent development, A typical day sees him eat eggs, salmon and dates for breakfast to match his insulin doses to the carbohydrates he’s taking on around 9.30am before training. Afterwards he’ll have a light lunch at 2pm then take something back from the training ground for a light evening meal.

In a recent development, ‘I just have to watch carbohydrates. I’ll eat more of them on match day but then work out my insulin ratio to the amount I eat and whether I need to inject more.

‘Adrenaline is higher on match days so that can change how you feel, I may inject four times before a night game and inject a bit more at half-time. If it’s not quite right you may get a bit heavy-legged or if I get a few cramps I may need a gel. But I've had no dangerous episodes.'.

When World Diabetes Day dawns on Saturday, O’Brien will be fully focused on preparing to play for Ireland in Austria in the Nations League.

O'Brien insists there was 'nothing in' reports that he wanted to leave Everton last summer to get more minutes at his preferred position of centre back.

At least O’Brien has former Everton captain Seamus Coleman on hand for advice.

Ireland assistant John O'Shea, a versatile defender himself in his Manchester United days, is another mentor. O’Shea and Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrímsson were at Hill Dickinson Stadium to watch O'Brien play his part in Everton's recent Carabao Cup win over Newcastle.

Recent findings suggest that 'Heimir is a good guy,' notes O'Brien. 'Very understanding. It's always a nice change of scenery to link up with Ireland. We've got a difficult couple of games (Austria and Kosovo) but hopefully if we get two wins it’s within reach.'.

Making his Hoffenheim debut against Werder Bremen on 31 October, Natnael Abraha (18) has since earned rave reviews from managing director of football Andreas Schicker.

Just five days after playing the full 90 minutes against Bremen, Abraha completed another 90 minutes in Hoffenheim’s 1-1 draw in the UEFA Europa League at English Premier League’s Crystal Palace.

“He has a great future ahead of him because he’s shown on the pitch what he brings to the table as a centre-back and right-back, both with and without the ball,” Schicker told Bild. “What I particularly like about him, though, is his humility, his down-to-earth nature, and his gratitude for being able to be part of the senior team. That’s why he received such an outstanding welcome from the team.”.

In a recent development, in training, Abraha has shown a willingness to learn. “Vladimír Coufal, also an extremely hard-working player and his direct competitor for the position, was practicing crosses after training. Natnael was passing him the balls,” explained Schicker, who lauded TSG’s rising star. “He observes carefully, how he crosses, how his standing foot is positioned, how he delivers the ball. He picked up quite a few things. That has to be emphasised, because nobody told him to do that, it came from him.

“It simply proves that the lad is down-to-earth and absolutely on the right track.”.

Born in Frankfurt, Abraha featured prominently for Germany’s U16 and U17 teams, bypassed the U18 squad and has earned six caps for the U19 squad after impressing for Hoffenheim II in the 3. Liga, where he’s made 18 appearances since January 2026.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Speaking ahead of the UEFA Nations League game against the Netherlands, German national team head coach Jürgen Klopp has called for a change in FIFA president.

“The consensus now is that a change would make sense,” he explained, further noting that people who don’t have a financial interest should take over the leadership at football’s governing body. “People thought things couldn’t get any worse after Sepp Blatter, and then we got this. There are certainly people who care about football and have no financial interests. If one of them became president, it would be absolutely helpful,” he added.

Recent findings suggest that current FIFA president Gianni Infantino has come under fire recently, especially following the 2026 FIFA World Cup. European nations, along with member associations from CONCACAF and Asia, have asked for him to leave his role, despite Infantino still maintaining strong support from African federations.

Among the decisions that increased the pressure on Infantino were details that emerged of an aborted proposal to create a commercial organization called FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) to manage commercial interests and sell minority stakes in tournaments like the World Cup to private investors, including a private investor group led by Joshua Kushner’s firm Thrive Capital.

This has caused opposition from UEFA, CONCACAF, and the Asian Football Confederation – which accused Infantino of breaking trust “through deception” and acting above the collective.

Infantino’s close relationship with US President Donald Trump also created controversy, as the FIFA peace prize was awarded to Trump and Florian Balogun’s ban following a red card was lifted at the World Cup following a call with the US President.

⏱️ ~23 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Xabi Alonso accused his Chelsea players of being “soft” after they failed to keep a clean sheet for the 20th successive Premier League game.
  • Chelsea threw away an early lead to draw 2-2 with Hull City and have conceded two or more goals in each of their four Premier League games.
  • Alonso has tried different systems and different players in those games, but suggested Chelsea’s biggest problem is mental.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Xabi Alonso accused his Chelsea players of being “soft” after they failed to keep a clean sheet for the 20th successive Premier League game.

Chelsea threw away an early lead to draw 2-2 with Hull City and have conceded two or more goals in each of their four Premier League games.

Alonso has tried different systems and different players in those games, but suggested Chelsea’s biggest problem is mental.

The club’s dreadful clean-sheet record pre-dates him and is the first time in 65 years Chelsea have gone 20 league games without keeping the opposition out.

Sources indicate that hull’s first goal from Mohamed Belloumi came after the ball had bounced over Jorrel Hato and Alonso said: “We need to be aware that from any situation, any team in the Premier League can hurt you. Today it was from a long ball, two bounces, the way it happened. You need to be very aware, very ready that the danger can come from any situation. If you are soft or if you are not prepared, you will get punished and we have been punished that way.”.

Chelsea have shared 30 goals with their opponents in the club’s six games in all competitions so far this season.

“Yeah, it’s all maybe entertaining, but I hope that one day you say it was a boring game and we win and we don’t give these entertaining moments,” he said.

Sources indicate that “But, for sure, it kind of repeats some patterns that we are making. It will take time to... or it will take moments to fix them when we get the lead and you still need to be competing and not give the chance so easily for them to come back, especially in the first goal, we can do much better.

“It was too soft to give them this hope because until then we were controlling, we were creating chances. But that momentum that we had changed the mood and the score of the game, and it’s something that we need to be talking [about], we address and we will get better. But it’s having an impact on our performances at the moment.”.

Asked if his players have a real desire to defend and keep clean sheets, Alonso remarked: “We can do better, we can do better for sure. We need to know that even when we have the lead, a very vital part of the game is to hold together, to keep the distance, to go intense in the situations to defend. I’m sure that we can do better.

Industry observers note that “Overall, I think that we are attacking better than defending in every part. We know that it’s a significant topic and a big theme for us. For sure, it’s just four games. But the dynamic in terms of conceding, I don’t like it and we need to do much better. Open play, set-pieces, long balls, this toughness, this competitive sense, we can do better.”.

Needing three goals or more to win games is not sustainable, as Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso is finding out.

This is not a problem of Alonso’s making, given Chelsea have now gone 20 Premier League games without a clean sheet. But he is certainly not improving the problem yet.

Chelsea beat Fulham with three goals and Brighton with four but left themselves far too much to do against Arsenal and were taken advantage of by Hull City, who will be slightly disappointed they did not leave Stamford Bridge with all three points.

Goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez has now conceded seven goals in three games since joining from Aston Villa, while central defender Maxence Lacroix, who joined for £52m from Crystal Palace in the summer, was relegated to the substitutes’ bench.

Martínez was at fault for Mohamed Belloumi’s second goal, but the Argentine did make a crucial save at his back post to stop substitute Mohamed-Ali Cho grabbing a winner that Chelsea could have had no complaints about.

Sources indicate that hull finished the game with more shots on goal than their hosts and a higher expected-goals rate. Chelsea are far too open and in some ways far too entertaining.

Defensive midfielder Moisés Caicedo cannot return from injury promptly enough, but this does not feel like a problem that will be solved by one man. Alonso needs to find a balance and instil a real desire in his team to defend.

Caicedo has that desire, but there are no defenders at the club who have shown that absolute desperation to keep the ball out of the net that Chelsea fans became so used to in the days of John Terry, Gary Cahill and César Azpilicueta.

Recent findings suggest that none of this should diminish Hull’s performance. They were not only spirited and full of character but also revealed quality and a threat. The joke is currently on those who laughed at their hopes of survival before a ball had been kicked.

According to recent reports, it is now two wins and two draws for Sergej Jakirovic’s team and they are already a fifth of the way to 40 points. Jakirovic had promised his staff a week off in the international break if they reached eight points after five games. With that target already met, there may be a fresh reward if Hull can make it 11 points against Newcastle United next weekend.

“Before the season, I mentioned to my staff that we will take seven, eight points in these first five and then I will give them seven days off,” Jakirovic said. “That was our target and now we are in a very good position, eight points.

“Especially today, it’s very, very difficult to play here, and now we will try to get even more. Of course, I’m a little bit worried about the international break because we have 13 national team players. But we will see who will come back and in what condition. So this is my concern right now.” Asked if his staff’s seven-day break will be extended if Hull can beat Newcastle, Jakirovic added: “I will tell them. But I know already.”.

While his five-game target may need modifying, Jakirovic is not deviating from his goal for the season for Hull. “Our target is always to stay in the league and collect as many points as possible,” he remarked. “Forty points, 38 to 41, this is the average we need. Then it’s easier to play. You can play more relaxed, with more joy and happiness. So [get to] this as soon as possible, so that we are safe.”.

Industry observers note that hull had not conceded a league goal before this and there had been predictions they might crumble when they finally let the ball into their net. They did so after just seven minutes but they kept their heads and came back stronger.

It was far too easy for Morgan Rogers to make a yard of space for himself to shoot after collecting the ball from João Pedro, and Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis may not have been happy to have been beaten at his near post.

Sources indicate that chelsea have now scored inside the first 10 minutes in all of their four league games, but Hull were in no mood to crumble and hit back with two goals in six minutes from Belloumi to take a half-time lead. Both Hull goals were shockers from Chelsea’s perspective. The first, in the 28th minute, came as a result of Jorrel Hato letting the ball bounce over him from a Ryan Giles cross and Belloumi finished brilliantly.

Belloumi’s second came after Martínez had flapped at a corner and Semi Ajayi had hit the bar with a header. The ball fell to Belloumi again and his shot was deflected into the net.

It was no surprise that Hato did not reappear for the second half, as he was replaced by Pep Chavarría at left-back. But Chelsea remained vulnerable and Martínez had to recover from spilling a Regan Slater shot to prevent Ollie McBurnie extending Hull’s advantage.

When Palmer and Pedro combined for Pedro to sweep the ball into the net and equalise with 24 minutes remaining, it seemed like it would be Chelsea who would provide the grandstand finish.

But it was Hull who got a second wind and Chelsea were indebted to Martínez for making a save to stop Cho securing all three points and sending the visiting fans home even happier.

I feel good. We have to be happy. It’s a huge result for us.

Sources indicate that we had 2-1 at half-time and we had a 100 per cent chance with McBurnie but Martinez’s save was excellent. We have to control play better in the box because we can stop this [Chelsea goal]. We had an excellent chance for Cho – Martinez saved again. Player of the match.

We can be very happy. We took a point in a very demanding match.

Eight points against very difficult opponents. We have to continue like this.

There have been 12 Premier League games at Anfield in 2026, Liverpool have only won 4 of them to date. This was seventh draw and Fulham deserves their share of the spoils. This was very much a learning experience for Andoni Iraola.

Not a single home win in the Premier League, today.

Aston Villa 1 Nottingham Forest 2Bournemouth 2 Brentford 2Chelsea 2 Hull City 2Crystal Palace 2 Ipswich Town 3Liverpool 0 Fulham 0.

What a result for Hull, who remain unbeaten and they have taken five points from fixtures against United, Villa and Chelsea.

That is the first really poor result of the Alonso era, points dropped.

What a thriller in SE25, both teams have been going for it in the closing stages, but Ipswich have surely score the winner through Zian Flemming.

It has been revealed that fulham were pointless before this game, but they have kept a clean sheet at Anfield with a disciplined display and they could well have score one or two. Underwhelming for Liverpool, who have not won just one of their first four games and their fixtures have not been the most taxing.

And as we predicted at the beginning of the game... Liverpool 0 Fulham 0. If this reporter ever gives you advice on a horse to back or a team to follow, make sure you take the opposite stance. Fulham deserve their reward and their fans are singing “We got a point!”.

Villa are finishing the game with 10 men because Ian Maatsen pulled up after Emery had made his five substitutions, and Forest have punished them through Igor Jesus with just a few minutes of normal time to play.

It has been revealed that alexander Isak heads over the bar when he perhaps should have hit the target. Has time run out for Liverpool?

You might imagine Chelsea are battering down the door, but Mohamed-Ali Cho has just forced Emi Martinez into a save at the other end. Hull will remain unbeaten if they can hold out.

Strand Larsen has had his critics, but he has scored his first goal of the season to set up a grandstand finish with 15 minutes plus stoppage time to play at Selhurst Park.

Short corner, McGinn whipped in an inswinging cross that is glanced into the bottom corner by Alysson.

In a recent development, liverpool continue to toil at Anfield, but no opening goal. Iraola has thrown on Frimpong, Mac Allister, Ngumoha and Gakpo in the second half. Fulham have had the chances to score at least one, and Josh King has just brought a save out of Alisson.

It has been revealed that hull are a little lucky they still have 11 men on the pitch. Already on a booking, my man Crooks bundled down Rogers. It could easily have been another yellow car but the referee let him off and now he’s been replaced by Iroegbunam.

Joao Pedro finds the smallest of gaps to be the goalkeeper and find the roof of the net with a brilliant, instinctive finish.

It has been revealed that that had not really been coming for Chelsea. It all felt a bit easy for Palmer to get his low cross into the box and Pedro to sweep the ball in. The home fans have woken up again.

Martinez was lucky to get away with another slip up, there. He spilt Slater’s shot but reacted before McBurnie to stop the Hull striker scoring the rebound. Just a day after his nasty looking crash, Sorba Thomas is on for Hull.

It has been revealed that this game is absolutely here for Fulham to win. Quietness has descended around Anfield, the hosts have no fluency in their play and Fulham are growing in confidence. Why wouldn’t they after getting to 65 minutes with a clean sheet?

Just like in the first half, four minutes after one of these teams taking the lead there has been an equaliser. Kevin Scahde is in a rich vein of form.

According to recent reports, bournemouth have have never beaten Brentford in the Premier League, but they might well be on their way to changing that record having trailed earlier in the game. Marcus Tavernier has just scored their second goal.

In a recent development, matt Davidson Rider Crooks has just been booked for a very cynical foul on Rogers. It gave Chelsea a free-kick in a dangerous position Reece James had an effort tipped away. Chelsea have started the second half well.

Within a minute of the restart, Villa lose the ball in midfield and Delap punishes them to the maximum. Cracking finish from just outside the box, and a much-needed goal by Delap. The Glasner curse striking for Emery again?

Liam Delap has just started paying back that £50m transfer fee with a fine goal.

Delap picked the ball up on the left and set himself up on the edge of the box before crashing a 25-yard shot past Zion Suzuki.

Unai Emery has made a couple of changes at half-time, taking off Nicolas Jackson who picked up a silly booking just before half-time.

Industry observers note that tammy Abraham is on in his place. George Hemmings is also off and replaced by Alysson.

It has been revealed that pep Chavarria on for Chelsea at half-time. He’s replaced Jorrel Hato, who had a bit of a stinker in the first half.

Andoni Iraola hasn’t hung about here. Milos Kerkez has come on immediately after half-time for Kostas Tsimikas and you can say with certainty that Liverpool will be shopping for a new left-back in due course.

According to recent reports, so at half-time, Hull City are top of the Premier League and don’t their supporters know it? They were singing “we are top of the League” for the full two minutes of time added on for stoppages at the end of the first period. Alonso has some work to do at the break.

Forest did need a brilliant double save from Matz Sels to deny Victor Lindelof and have recovered to slow the match down.

Neco Williams wasted a decent chance for Forest from outside the penalty area shortly before the break.

Referee Andrew Madley has irritated both teams with a number of weird decisions - but that’s sadly par for the course with officials nowadays.

Villa 0 Forest 0Bournemouth 1 Brentford 1Chelsea 1 Hull City 2Palace 1 Ipswich 2Liverpool 0 Fulham 0.

Palace in some trouble now, level with Ipswich and down to 10 men. Disasi was sent off in the 34th minute for a reckless challenge on Jack Clarke, caught him with studs on shin.

Things got worse for Palace just before half-time, with Leif Davis heading home at the back post to give Ipswich the league.

Industry observers note that apologies for the lack of updates, some technical gremlins at Telegraph Towers. A nip and tuck game as expected at at the Vitality: Kevin Schade gave Brentford the lead before Justin Kluivert equalised four minutes later.

One way to put it is that Kostas Tsimikas isn’t playing well. Another way to say it would be that his efforts are making Milos Kerkez look like Roberto Carlos. The Greek left-back is having a dreadful afternoon and Fulham are getting plenty of joy out of him. We suggested there was no chance of this game finishing goalless, and it’s anomalous that we have reached 40 minutes without score. Fulham, certainly, have a sense of adventure and have been into Liverpool’s 18-yard box plenty of times. Let’s see if the picture changes before the interval.

In a recent development, that’s now seven goals Emi Martinez has conceded in three games since joining from Villa to supposedly solve Chelsea’s goalkeeping crisis. Martinez won’t be pleased with Hull’s second goal, here. He was beaten to a corner by Ajayi. His header hit the bar and Belloumi’s shot was deflected past him. The Hull fans are in dreamland.

This is a turn up for the books. Chelsea undone by a long ball forward, and Hato lets the ball bounce over his head, and Belloumi finishes with aplomb.

Sources indicate that that’s now 20 Premier League games Chelsea have gone without keeping a clean sheet. What an earth was Jorrel Hato doing, letting the ball bounce over him for Belloumi? Amateur stuff at the back from the home side. It was Hull’s first meaningful attack.

Emersonn has struggled in some games so far this season, but he has just planted a header into the corner from a Davis cross.

There is a VAR check for offside... but the goal stands.

Sources indicate that 5 - Morgan Rogers is the fifth different player to score or assist in each of Chelsea's first four games of a Premier League season, after Didier Drogba (2010-11), Cesc Fàbregas (2014-15), Diego Costa (2014-15 & 2016-17), and Eden Hazard (2018-19).Famous. pic.twitter.com/0cuThzH472.

Industry observers note that A sweet strike from one of Palace’s summer signings, recruited from Union Saint Gilloise, and that is his first Palace goal. The 22-year-old Israeli came through at Maccabi Haifa. Uphill task for Gary O’Neill and Ipswich.

Sources indicate that austin MacPhee, Chelsea’s flamboyant set-piece coach, just motioned for Xabi Alonso to sit down when the Blues manager momentarily got up from his seat when the home side were preparing to take a corner. It seems MacPhee wears the (correct length) trousers when it comes to set pieces.

It has been revealed that an almighty let off for Alisson and Liverpool after pass from the goalkeeper played Gravenberch into trouble, but Jacquet cleared off the line to keep the game goalless. That was Fulham’s first foray forward.

A bright start in this game and there is no chance it will end goalless (famous last words). Andoni Iraola has made three changes from the team that beat Atletico Madrid on Wednesday and it’s a pattern of his early management that he is making the kind of decisions that supporters are nodding along in approval with. Liverpool should already be one up but Alexander Isak’s shot has just drifted across the face of goal but the signs are encouraging. It could be a long afternoon for Alvaro Arbeloa.

Industry observers note that wow. Unbelievable double save from Forest’s Matz Sels there to keep out Victor Lindelof.

The first was the most impressive, a reflex stop after a deflection.

Recent findings suggest that morgan Rogers is the first player to score against Hull City this season. Emi Martinez rolled out the ball forward after claiming a corner, and Rogers’ shot from the edge of the area crept under the goalkeeper Tzolakis. He will not want to watch that one again.

In a recent development, we’re past five minutes and it’s the longest Chelsea have gone without scoring in the league this season. Back on Matt Crooks – one of his middle names is Rider.

It has been revealed that although Rogers scored in the seventh minute...so the early goals continue for Chelsea. It will be difficult for Hull now.

Twelve seconds in and the chant “where were you in Istanbul” gets a very early airing from Villa’s home fans.

That is of course a reference to Villa’s 4-0 win over Forest in the Europa League semi-final second leg last season.

The early indications are that Reece James is playing in midfield with Malo Gusto at right-back in a conventional back four.

Sources indicate that xabi Alonso has made an encouraging start to life as Chelsea manager. But his trousers upset me. They are three inches too short and a bit baggy above the ankle.

We are under way in the five Premier League 3pm kick-offs. Goals and further updates from around the grounds as they happen.

Some early #analysis from Matt at the Bridge, about one of Hull’s midfielders.

Matt Crooks is absolutely massive.

One player who has really shone for Villa so far this season is teenage midfielder George Hemmings.

Unai Emery has been very impressed with the academy graduate, who made his Champions League debut on Tuesday night.

There is also a big buzz around £51m signing Johan Manzambi, who is on the bench today after recovering from a knee injury.

According to recent reports, will we get another fast start from Chelsea today? They have scored inside the first five minutes in all three of their League games this season. Hull are yet to concede.

Industry observers note that dominic King writes that there were signs of promise in the relationship between Barcola, Wirtz and Isak in Liverpool’s win over Atletico Madrid, and all three forwards start against Fulham. Timothy Castagne, Fulham’s right-back will need to have his sprinting boots on against Barcola, who is grease lightning.

Hull are really tough to beat. They have played against some good opponents and they’ve kept them out - they haven’t conceded yet. It is going to be difficult because they are really organised but we are at home and it is on us to make the game about us.

We know it is always tough against Brentford. We can expect a tight game today, definitely. We both want to win so it’ll be a nice game.

Sources indicate that we are very excited about our first European game coming up but we haven’t really spoken about it lately because we have just spoken about this game. This is a major game and we are looking for our first three points of the season. We have been close in every game so we hope to get it today.

Unai Emery is possibly the best coach in the Premier League but has found past encounters with Oliver Glasner very uncomfortable.

Since Glasner’s arrival in English football with Crystal Palace in February 2024, he has faced Emery’s Villa seven times and never lost.

With five victories and two draws, it is an impressive record albeit with a different set of players.

Aston Villa and Forest are two teams in transition, and meet for the first time since that two-legged Europa League semi-final last season.

Villa are building a latest chapter after a summer of significant change, while Forest are implementing a totally different style of play under Oliver Glasner.

There have been signs of progress at both of the former European Cup winners. Villa secured an impressive victory over Club Brugge in the Champions League on Tuesday. Forest are improving under Glasner, with their best performance the 2-2 draw at Liverpool.

Returning to Villa Park will have some bitter memories for a number of the Forest players, after that 4-0 defeat in the second leg of the Europa League.

Ollie Watkins and Emi Martinez departed for pastures latest in the transfer window.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this afternoon’s Premier League three o’clock kick-offs, and home bankers would appear to be the theme of the day.

Liverpool will be strongly fancied to put Fulham to the sword at Anfield, with confidence low at the London club and upcoming manager Alvaro Arbeloa (once a player at Anfield) already under pressure amid reports of dressing room unrest. Andoni Iraola secured his first Premier League victory as Liverpool manager at Ipswich last time out, and backed up that result with a come-from-behind win against Atletico Madrid in the Champions League.

Sources indicate that chelsea host Hull City, who are unbeaten after three games and have yet to concede a goal. It is a remarkable start to the season for Sergej Jakirović‘s side, who continue to defy expectations as well as the underlying data. For all their spirit and defensive organisation, keeping out Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro at Stamford Bridge promises to be a tall order, though.

Aston Villa’s rocky start to the campaign took a turn for the better with a 3-2 Champions League victory at Club Brugge, and as the weeks go by Unai Emery’s team should grow stronger as their raft of young signings bed in. Nottingham Forest could be obdurate opponents, although Villa swept them aside in the second leg of last season’s Europa League semi-final. Oliver Glasner’s Crystal Palace were a bogey team for Villa though, with the Austrian coach undefeated against Emery having notched up some resounding victories.

Glasner’s former club Palace could do with a home win against Ipswich Town, while there is cigarette paper between Bournemouth and Brentford, two of the league’s smartest operators who play at the Vitality Stadium this afternoon. Bournemouth qualified for Europe at Brentford’s expense last season, but Marco Rose is looking for his first league win despite some encouraging performances.

Scegli Fcinter1908.it come tuo sito preferito su Google: clicca qui.

Intervistato da La Gazzetta dello Sport, l’ex bomber dell’Inter Alessandro Altobelli ha parlato dell’ascesa di Pio Esposito e del reparto offensivo nerazzurro:.

«Quello dell’Inter è il migliore attacco d’Italia».

Come valuta i numeri offensivi dell’Inter fin qui?

Industry observers note that «Benissimo, la squadra ha un attacco molto forte e soprattutto per Chivu c’è la possibilità di cambiare interpreti a seconda dei momenti dei singoli. Lautaro e Thuram sono fortissimi, Pio Esposito e Bonny forti. Per un allenatore avere l’imbarazzo della scelta è una grandissima fortuna: se qualcuno dovesse riposare, il tecnico avrebbe altre certezze. Tutti e 4 gli attaccanti dell’Inter farebbero gola a qualsiasi squadra italiana, giocherebbero titolari ovunque».

Il suo percorso è simile a quello di Esposito, entrambi siete cresciuti a Brescia. Come valuta Pio?

Industry observers note that «Conosco suo papà da un pezzo, anche tutti i suoi fratelli. Sono persone serie, oneste e dei grandi professionisti. Tengono molto alle squadre per cui giocano. So bene il valore del Pio di oggi e soprattutto quello che potrà dare in futuro. Con lui, l’Inter ha trovato l’attaccante ideale. E poi è giovanissimo, pensi per quanti anni ancora potrà giocare da protagonista...».

Ha notato differenze tra Inter e Nazionale per quanto riguarda l’apporto di Pio?

It has been revealed that «No, mi pare sia lo stesso in entrambe le realtà. Anzi, credo sia logico che allenandosi tutti i giorni con l’Inter gli venga naturale trovare un’intesa maggiore con i compagni di squadra nerazzurri. L’importante è che, come fa, ovunque vada lasci il segno: sempre pronto al momento giusto, forte di testa, negli anticipi, sia di destro che di sinistro».

Lautaro, Thuram, Pio, Bonny: la scelta non manca.

Industry observers note that «È vero, sono in tanti, ma l’Inter gioca il campionato, la Champions, la Coppa Italia, la Supercoppa. Quindi lo spazio è importante per tutti. Una squadra come l’Inter deve avere molti attaccanti forti. La storia dimostra che quando c’è una sola punta che deve giocare tutte le partite, poi i problemi arrivano. Lautaro è il più forte di tutti, ma in questo momento Thuram è spaventoso mentre Pio e Bonny rappresentano due belle novità».

L’attacco di Chivu è il più forte d’Italia?

«Sì. Sono tutti bravi e complementari. Anche Milan, Roma e Napoli ne hanno di forti, ma la differenza nel far rendere meglio i propri la fa il resto della squadra, che è più forte. All’Inter sono tutti bravi, anche il portiere che costruisce, i difensori e i centrocampisti, che creano tanto e lavorano molto affinché le punte rendano al meglio».

Un organico profondo come quello nerazzurro sarà determinante anche per andare avanti in Champions League?

According to recent reports, «C’è stata una partenza un po’ a rilento, ma le squadre contro cui l’Inter ha giocato all’inizio si trovavano, in quel momento, in una condizione atletica migliore. È quello il motivo per cui l’Inter ha sofferto un po’. Ma la squadra ha già dimostrato che ci sono spazio e tempo per recuperare».

Vede l’Inter favorita anche per quanto riguarda il campionato?

Industry observers note that «Assolutamente, nonostante la Lazio stia ancora resistendo penso che l’Inter sia la favorita numero uno. Certo, ci sono anche la Roma, il Milan, la stessa squadra di Gattuso. Però i nerazzurri, con un attacco così...».

Harry Kane had to compose himself and hold back the tears while reading beautiful letters from his children after breaking the England appearance record.

The 33-year-old earned his 126th cap and scored in the 2-1 win over Croatia on Thursday night, with the Wembley crowd celebrating his achievement and Ballon d'Or triumph.

And on the following morning, there was a surprise in store for the England skipper, who was visibly taken aback on camera when presented with letters from his four children, nine-year-old Ivy, eight-year-old Vivi, five-year-old Louis and three-year-old Henry, who he shares with wife Kate.

'Wow, that’s uh a bit of a surprise,' Kane noted as he examined the letters and artwork. 'I think you guys are trying to make me cry on camera.'.

He opened the first one before reading aloud: 'To Daddy, I love you very much and I want you to know that I’m very proud of you and also you are the best footballer in the world, the most kind Daddy in the world and the best striker in the world.

'I would like to celebrate you playing the most games for England by holiday together and eating ice cream.

Harry Kane was on the verge of tears as he read touching letters from his four children.

In a recent development, 'My favorite thing about you is you never give up and I love all things you do for us. Love Ivy.'.

Dewy-eyed Kane then reflected: 'I wasn’t expecting this beautiful letter. Thank you Ivy. I love you. I've got one here from Vivian as well.'.

Sources indicate that 'Dear Daddy, I’m so happy and proud of you. I love you because you are hard working and make the best fried eggs. I want to celebrate with you by going fishing, going down the water slides and having a cinema trip as well. Love from Vivi.'.

Recent findings suggest that kane then said: 'Yeah, you’ve caught me by surprise here to be honest with you. I’m trying to just uh, stay strong for the camera. Thank you Vivi, love you.'.

Then came the letters from Kane's two sons, Louis and Henry.

Louis' read: 'To Daddy, I love you so much because you train and work so hard. My favorite thing we do together is play football and cricket together. I love when you play England football because you score goals and we get to sing Vindaloo. I want to celebrate with you by making an ice cream house with sweets inside. Love Louis.'.

It has been revealed that 'Thank you Louie, love you, boy. This last one is from Henry,' Kane remarked.

Industry observers note that the short and sweet note from his youngest went: 'Daddy, you are the winner. Vindaloo! Love Henry.'.

Kane walked onto the pitch with his children, (L-R) Henry, Ivy, Vivi, Louis on Thursday night.

Kane showed the artwork and hand-written letters to the camera as he read them.

In a recent development, kane then pointed the endearing scribble to the camera, saying: 'He’s drawn me a lovely picture there. Love you, Henry. Thank you, beautiful messages from my wonderful family.'.

Kane, who lives with his family in Bavaria and recently signed a fresh deal worth £400,000-a-week at Bayern Munich, brought the whole clan, including his parents, to Wembley for his big night on Thursday.

He walked out onto the hallowed turf with his four children, admired a gigantic tifo of himself in the crowd, posed for pictures with the gleaming Ballon d'Or trophy and was given a commemorative shirt by Prince William.

Kane is a devoted family man in addition to being the world's best footballer and took a moment to say a few words about his children at the Ballon d'Or ceremony last month.

He mentioned: 'To Ivy, Vivienne, Louis and Henry. You're the reason I do this.

Prince William presented Kane with a commemorative framed shirt with 126 on the back.

'I don't think you'll fully maybe appreciate bringing this trophy home. I'll bring a few others home, but this one is a special one, so I can't wait to see you and celebrate with you.

'I want to set a good example being a father but also being a professional and what it means to work hard, what it means to believe in yourself. I love you very much.'.

Kane passed Peter Shilton as the record appearance-maker for England on Thursday and took his tally of goals for the national team to 92.

His penalty put England 2-1 up and they would not relinquish their lead. He'll next be in action against Spain on Sunday.

Sources indicate that all’interno del bilancio della SSC Napoli chiuso al 30 giugno 2026 c’è un paragrafo dedicato alle previsioni per la stagione successiva. Di seguito, l’estratto:.

“Il prossimo esercizio di attività della Società vedrà la prima squadra militare nel campionato di Serie A, nella Coppa Italia e nella UEFA Champions League. Le strategie di crescita definite dalla Società sono ancora attuali e pertanto si continuerà a puntare sia allo sviluppo delle attività esistenti sia ad investire ulteriormente su settori capaci di generare proventi aggiuntivi quali la produzione e distribuzione diretta del c.d. merchandising. Per la stagione 2026/2027 è comunque previsto che la Società continui ad operare sul mercato dei diritti alle prestazioni sportive di calciatori con l’obiettivo di efficientare e razionalizzare il comparto sportivo preservando il grado di competitività della squadra. L’entità degli investimenti sarà, come sempre, oggetto di attenta analisi sotto il profilo della complessiva sostenibilità economicofinanziaria, nell’ambito della citata strategia di razionalizzazione del parco giocatori, anche in considerazione dei vincoli imposti dalla regolamentazione F.I.G.C. con riferimento all’Indicatore del Costo del Lavoro Allargato e alla Regola del Pareggio di Bilancio, e UEFA con riferimento al c.d. financial sustainability regulation. Valutati i ricavi che saranno prodotti attraverso la partecipazione della prima squadra al Campionato di Serie A, alla Coppa Italia e alla UEFA Champions League, ed anche tenendo conto che talune delle variabili economiche connesse alla determinazione del risultato atteso per l’esercizio in corso sono, per definizione, difficilmente stimabili (effetti derivanti dalla finestra invernale del c.d. “calciomercato”, andamento dei risultati sportivi, ecc.), considerato il livello degli investimenti in essere nonché i possibili effetti sul ciclo economico generale connessi all’evoluzione dei conflitti in Ucraina ed in Medio Oriente, si può ragionevolmente ipotizzare che l’andamento economico della Società a fine periodo possa esprimere sostenibilità a medio termine garantendo comunque l’integrità del patrimonio netto della stessa nonostante la previsione di una perdita di esercizio”.

Six games into Jürgen Klopp's tenure as Germany coach, Bild has shed light on how the national team's central midfield options are right now ranked.

Perhaps unsurprisingly, given that they started together in a double pivot in the recent 3-1 win over Serbia and 5-0 thrashing of the Netherlands, Germany captain Joshua Kimmich tops the list ahead of Bayern Munich teammate Aleksandar Pavlović.

Another Bayern player, Tom Bischof, occupies third place after coming on as the first midfield substitute in both games. The 21-year-old has moved ahead of Felix Nmecha, who was a starter under Julian Nagelsmann at the World Cup but managed just nine minutes of playing time across the two November fixtures.

Celtic's Mika Baur is ranked fifth despite missing out on the latest squad. The midfielder was reportedly first on the standby list in case of an injury and is understood to be highly regarded by Klopp.

Finally, Leeds United's Anton Stach is named as the sixth option. Klopp tested the former Hoffenheim player as a substitute in two matches in September and continues to monitor his performances in the Premier League.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that SC Freiburg attacker Derry Scherhant enjoyed an unforgettable evening in his hometown of Berlin on Monday, scoring Germany’s opening goal in a commanding 5-0 Nations League victory over the Netherlands. The 24-year-old subsequently reflected on his unlikely journey to the national team and took particular satisfaction in proving those who had once questioned his ability to become a professional footballer wrong.

According to recent reports, scherhant had arranged approximately 50 tickets for family members and friends ahead of the encounter at the Olympiastadion. The former Hertha BSC youngster, who grew up just five minutes from the venue, marked the occasion with an outstanding individual performance and a spectacular first-half goal.

Scherhant opened the scoring in the 41st minute after receiving a pass from Joshua Kimmich, cutting inside and dispatching a powerful effort into the upper-right corner. The Freiburg professional had already struck the outside of the post earlier in the half and subsequently played a decisive role in Germany’s fifth goal.

The performance represented another significant milestone in a remarkable international breakthrough that has gathered momentum since Jürgen Klopp took charge of the German national team.

Recent findings suggest that as Get German Football News detailed in its comprehensive October feature on Scherhant’s unusual career trajectory, the winger’s development was anything but straightforward. Scherhant struggled to establish himself at Viktoria Berlin and Tennis Borussia before eventually finding his way into Hertha BSC’s academy in 2020. His early difficulties included repeated questions about his physical development and whether he possessed the necessary qualities to succeed at the professional level.

He ultimately earned a Bundesliga debut with Hertha, although regular opportunities remained elusive during the club’s turbulent relegation campaign in 2022/23. The subsequent spell in the 2. Bundesliga proved notable to his development, and SC Freiburg eventually secured his services in the summer of 2025. The move to Breisgau provided Scherhant with a more stable environment, even if initially displacing established attacker Vincenzo Grifo presented another considerable challenge.

GGFN‘s 2026/27 tactical preview of SC Freiburg identified Scherhant as one of the club’s most impressive performers during preseason preparations. The former Hertha attacker subsequently consolidated his place in Julian Schuster’s starting XI.

A particularly impressive Bundesliga performance against Eintracht Frankfurt followed his first senior Germany nomination in September. Scherhant contributed a goal and an assist in the 2-2 draw, providing further evidence of his rapid development.

Sources indicate that the remarkable progression continued at international level. Scherhant earned his senior Germany debut during Klopp’s first international window and impressed sufficiently to retain his place when the Bundestrainer reduced his squad ahead of November’s fixtures. Get German Football News subsequently reported on Scherhant and Freiburg teammate Philipp Treu’s appreciation of the supportive environment at their Bundesliga club. Both players credited Freiburg’s collective mentality and stable working conditions with helping them establish themselves at international level.

In a recent development, scherhant also spoke enthusiastically about the prospect of representing Germany in Berlin. The winger celebrated his 24th birthday during the November international break and regarded the opportunity to return to the Olympiastadion as an extraordinary personal occasion. His performance against the Netherlands ultimately exceeded even those expectations.

The Freiburg attacker became only the third Berlin-born player to score for Germany in an international match staged in the capital, following Thomas Häßler against Bulgaria in November 1995 and Hans Ruch against Scotland in June 1929.

It has been revealed that klopp was particularly impressed by the contributions of Scherhant and fellow attacker Brajan Gruda. The Bundestrainer praised not only their technical abilities but also the considerable defensive work and intensity they contributed to Germany’s convincing victory.

Speaking after Monday’s victory, Scherhant recalled how frequently his chances of reaching professional football had been dismissed during his youth.

It has been revealed that “A few years ago, people told me that I wouldn’t make it as a professional,” Scherhant explained. “Then I became a professional. And even then, some people were still saying that it wasn’t enough, that the Regionalliga was the highest level I’d ever reach. It’s simply unbelievable that I’m now standing here, with the satisfaction of having proved those people wrong. 99 percent would have said never. One percent might have said perhaps, if he works really hard.”.

Klopp offered his own assessment of Scherhant’s contribution alongside Gruda.

“Derry Scherhant and Brajan Gruda, the way those two play football — my goodness,” Klopp remarked afterwards. “But the amount of work they put in and had to put in today was extraordinary. That’s what ultimately makes a team. Because there are other players who can play football too. But it’s the commitment and passion you bring to it that ultimately matter.”.

Scherhant himself struggled to contain his delight after scoring in the stadium he once called home.

“What can I say?” Scherhant said. “It couldn’t have gone any better, scoring the opening goal here in my own city. You couldn’t have dreamed it up any better. It’s truly unbelievable. I had a tremendous amount of fun and I’m simply overjoyed.”.

With his postponed birthday celebrations still awaiting him, Scherhant could finally look forward to an evening with family and friends after a homecoming that will remain among the most memorable moments of his young career.

Usman Nurmagomedov and his entourage have been swiftly punished with prison sentences and fines in Abu Dhabi after their shocking hotel attack.

Nurmagomedov set upon UFC star Merab Dvalishvili on Wednesday, slapping him in the lobby of Yas Hilton hotel in a revenge mission filmed by his friends.

The Georgian-American Dvalishvili then retaliated and fought back with his cameraman as the melee rapidly descended into complete mayhem. Dvalishvili was left bloodied and bruised and the attackers were quickly detained by the authorities.

In just two days, their punishments have been decided by the Abu Dhabi Judicial Department, who published the findings on social media.

Six of the attackers were given six-month prison sentences and ordered to pay £61,000 each in fines. They will also be immediately deported  when their sentences end.

They were described as having 'caused panic, disturbed public security and  endangered lives'.

Two of Nurmagomedov's associates were fined £10,000 each for 'disturbing public security and assaulting others'.

Usman Nurmagomedov (left) was the one who initiated the brawl by slapping Merab Dvalishvili - his brother Umar (right) lost a title shot against the Georgian last year.

The Abu Dhabi court shared this post online confirming the punishments for the attackers.

And the other two members of the group who recorded the assault were given six-month sentences, £61,000 fines and confiscation of the devices used.

They were punished 'for violating privacy by using information technology to film and publish footage of the brawl'.

Dvalishvili had been due to fight in a RAF wrestling event on Saturday. CEO and co-founder Chad Bronstein released a statement confirming the fighter is back.

In a recent development, he said: 'I am pleased to share that Merab Dvalishvili is back with us in Abu Dhabi. We would like to express our sincere appreciation to the relevant authorities in Abu Dhabi for their professionalism and support.

'We remain focused on moving forward and are pleased to have Merab back with us.'.

Nurmagomedov and his team's violent ambush was four months in the making.

Back in July, Dvalishvili was competing in a RAF event in Georgia, which is a freestyle wrestling show the UFC allow their fighters to compete in outside of the day job.

While milling around at the event, a Dagestani wrestler and friend of Umar, Ahmed Gadzhimagomedov, confronted Dvalishvili about refusing to entertain a rematch of any kind with Umar.

UFC star Merab Dvalishvili was attacked in a five-star hotel in Abu Dhabi on Wednesday.

'I was super relaxed, super chilled and then somebody (Gadzhimagomedov) came and grabbed my neck and pulled me over and started yelling at me in Russian language, which I hardly understand,' Dvalishvili told Ariel Helwani.

In a recent development, 'And he mentioned Umar. It took me a couple of seconds to realize, "Who is this guy to tell me what to talk about him?".

According to recent reports, 'It’s between me and Umar… I have so much respect for all Dagestani people, especially fighters. The only guy who I don't like from Dagestan is Umar and his sneaky manager, Rizvan. The guy who was helping Umar disrespect me on X and Threads.'.

After Gadzhimagomedov squared up to him, Dvalishvili shoved him in the neck, shouting: 'What's your problem, b***h!'.

The situation, unlike the hotel brawl that escalated into a complete bloodbath, was swiftly defused and there was a child in close proximity.

Usman wanted to take revenge on behalf of fellow Dagestani Gadzhimagomedov and also his brother Umar, who lost against Dvalishvili in a title shot last year.

In the footage of the hotel attack, the group appeared to approach Dvalishvili, 35, from behind, before one man remarked a couple of words to him and slapped him in the face.

Dvalishvili was rocked, then kicked, and was held back by a man he appeared to be with.

He tried to fight back but a number of men overwhelmed him as his companion was attacked too. Eventually, the groups were separated, and Dvalishvili took to social media to respond to the incident.

The 35-year-old was blind sided while carrying out an interview.

He mentioned in a video, bloody and bruised as he received treatment: 'What a sneaky way guys. Just two of us, me and my friend, came here in Abu Dhabi and Usman and his friends came like snakes from behind. What kind of fighters are you guys? What kind of man does this? If you want to fight, let's do it the real way.

According to recent reports, 'You guys came when there was two of us, you were prepared. What the f***.'.

Recent findings suggest that his companion then added: 'From behind? You call yourselves men? You're a little b***h.'.

Dvalishvili continued: 'You are sneaky guys. You are not real men. It shows your guys' character, what the f*** guys? If you want to fight, let's fight. We are fighters. I talk straight, but you guys came from behind. I don't know how many guys, all your friends waiting for us in a sneaky way, wow.

Recent findings suggest that 'I knew guys, I knew what kind of guys you were. Usman, Umar and his friends came sneaky from behind, so many guys. Wow. I am fine guys. All my friends and family, I am f***ing fine. I am a fighter. This is nothing for me, but it shows what kind of people you guys are. P***ys do this bro. We are warriors.'.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to Kicker, an average of 10.35 million viewers watched the UEFA Nations League encounter live on German public broadcaster ARD.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Germany’s commanding 5-0 victory over the Netherlands on Monday evening attracted an enormous television audience, with more than ten million viewers tuning in to watch Jürgen Klopp’s national team deliver their most convincing performance of the November international break.

According to Kicker, an average of 10.35 million viewers watched the UEFA Nations League encounter live on German public broadcaster ARD. The figure translated into an impressive 42.3 percent share of the overall television market.

Sources indicate that the numbers were even more striking among the commercially relevant advertising demographic. Some 2.8 million viewers in this category followed Germany’s emphatic victory, accounting for a remarkable 54.3 percent market share.

Industry observers note that the substantial television audience complemented an equally impressive turnout in Berlin. A sold-out Olympiastadion welcomed 71,765 spectators, who witnessed Germany record their second-largest victory over their Dutch rivals. Only the historic 7-0 triumph in 1959 exceeded Monday’s five-goal margin.

The result also marked another significant step forward for Klopp, whose November squad selection featured several younger players who had impressed during his first international window.

Monday’s audience figures also compare interestingly with Germany’s earlier 1-1 draw against the Netherlands during Klopp’s first international window.

That encounter, broadcast by RTL, attracted 10.63 million viewers during the first half, representing a 43.7 percent market share. The audience subsequently rose to 10.76 million in the second half, with the market share climbing to 50.6 percent.

While those figures represent individual halves rather than a full-match average, both encounters illustrate the considerable television audiences generated by Germany’s Nations League meetings with their longstanding rivals.

Monday’s resounding victory offered those watching from home and those attending in Berlin a particularly memorable evening as Germany secured their place in the Nations League quarter-finals.

#15059. FEATURE | Seven winners from Germany’s November 2026 international break
