FEATURE | Seven winners from Germany’s November 2026 international break

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 18 min read (3580 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Getfootballnewsgermany

⏱️ ~18 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The German national team concluded its 2026 international calendar with two impressive UEFA Nations League victories, securing passage to the quarter-finals as group winners and supplying supporters with considerably more reasons for optimism than seemed possible during Jürgen Klopp’s first assignments as Bundestrainer.
  • A convincing 3-1 victory over Serbia in Belgrade on Friday preceded an extraordinary 5-0 dismantling of the Netherlands in Berlin on Monday.
  • Sources indicate that the contrast with September is particularly striking.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The German national team concluded its 2026 international calendar with two impressive UEFA Nations League victories, securing passage to the quarter-finals as group winners and supplying supporters with considerably more reasons for optimism than seemed possible during Jürgen Klopp’s first assignments as Bundestrainer. Germany once again find themselves in the ascendancy.

Well then. What a difference a month makes!

A convincing 3-1 victory over Serbia in Belgrade on Friday preceded an extraordinary 5-0 dismantling of the Netherlands in Berlin on Monday. Eight goals, six points, and first place in Group A2. The results alone would have sufficed to declare November a success. The manner in which Germany accomplished all of this, however, offers far more interesting material for analysis.

Sources indicate that the contrast with September is particularly striking. Get German Football News spent much of Klopp’s first international window documenting the considerable difficulties encountered during his experimental 44-player squad selection. An uninspiring 1-1 draw against the Netherlands and a frustrating 1-0 home defeat to Greece left many questions unanswered.

Germany gradually improved during the October assignments. Klopp’s first victory over Serbia finally offered tangible evidence of the collective intensity and positional flexibility he wanted to establish. The subsequent scoreless draw in Greece nevertheless made evident that there remained plenty of work to do.

November supplied considerably stronger evidence of progress.

Against Serbia, Germany controlled 79 percent of possession, attempted 22 shots, and generated 3.57 expected goals according to Opta match data. The overmatched hosts rarely managed to disrupt Germany’s midfield rhythm during the opening 45 minutes, while the visitors created enough opportunities to have settled the encounter well before the interval.

Recent findings suggest that the Netherlands presented a considerably more demanding assignment. Xavi Hernandez’s side arrived in Berlin having scored seven goals against Greece and needed to be beaten if Germany were to guarantee progression.

It has been revealed that it took some time for the Germans to gain control of the contest. The Dutch created several dangerous transition situations early on, and Germany’s aggressive positioning occasionally left the defensive line exposed. By the conclusion of the match, however, the visitors had been completely overwhelmed.

Perhaps even more significantly, Klopp appeared to have settled upon a more consistent tactical structure.

According to recent reports, having experimented with several formations during his opening assignments, the Bundestrainer deployed the same basic 4-1-4-1 in both November matches. The arrangement placed Joshua Kimmich at the base of midfield, with Aleksandar Pavlovic and Florian Wirtz operating further forward. Brajan Gruda and Derry Scherhant supplied the wide attacking threat, while Kai Havertz led the line.

Industry observers note that the personnel changed little between Belgrade and Berlin. The results, however, provided further confirmation that Germany’s emerging system can accommodate both established internationals and the players Klopp has introduced.

We now turn to the seven footballers who benefited most from this remarkable conclusion to the 2026 international calendar.

According to recent reports, as usual, the selections appear in descending order from strongest to weakest. Goals and assists obviously count for plenty, but so too do tactical contributions, consistency, and the extent to which individual players have taken advantage of the opportunities afforded them.

Industry observers note that some of the choices are rather straightforward. Others require a broader assessment of the player’s place in Klopp’s squad hierarchy. A footballer need not deliver two spectacular performances to emerge from an international break in a stronger position than the one he occupied beforehand.

The author shall endeavor to defend all seven selections.

In a recent development, one suspects that even the most optimistic observers of Gruda’s development could scarcely have envisioned a more productive first two senior international appearances. The 22-year-old arrived in November as one of the few remaining uncapped members of Klopp’s original Germany selection. Injury had deprived him of his first opportunity during the previous international window, despite the Bundestrainer having already identified him as a player of considerable interest.

Industry observers note that as GGFN reported following Gruda’s impressive Champions League performance against PSV Eindhoven in October, Klopp had personally encouraged the youngster to remain patient, assuring him that a postponed debut did not necessarily mean a cancelled opportunity. That opportunity arrived in Belgrade, where Gruda immediately demonstrated the qualities that prompted Klopp to include him.

Industry observers note that operating on the right wing, the Leipzig attacker mixed direct running and technically ambitious dribbling with the occasional ill-advised attempt to beat too many opponents. Some questionable decisions and a deserved yellow card reflected the understandable exuberance of a player making his international debut.

The early signs were nevertheless encouraging. Gruda’s excellent delivery from the right in the 19th minute should have provided Havertz with a goal, although the Arsenal striker failed to connect properly with the cross. The youngster’s defining contribution arrived five minutes after the restart.

Recent findings suggest that released by Kimmich from deep in Germany’s half, Gruda embarked on a sensational solo run across approximately half the pitch before finishing past Vanja Milinkovic-Savic. Serbian defenders offered rather limited resistance along the way, but there could be no disputing the ambition and execution of the individual effort.

According to recent reports, gruda’s first international goal effectively secured Germany’s victory. The Leipzig professional saved his finest overall performance for Berlin. Once again deployed on the right, Gruda repeatedly attacked his opponents in one-on-one situations. His first-half work wasn’t entirely free of inaccuracies, but the second 45 brought a spectacular combination of invention and productivity.

According to recent reports, an excellent diagonal pass from Schlotterbeck presented Gruda with another opportunity to cut inside and shoot shortly after the restart. The winger continued searching for openings before taking over as one of Germany’s principal creative forces.

Gruda delivered the free kick from which Schlotterbeck headed Germany’s third goal, supplied Wirtz with an excellent opportunity to score the fourth, and completed the scoring himself after Scherhant’s effort rebounded off the post.

One goal and two assists against the Netherlands. Two goals and two assists across his first two senior internationals.

The numbers are impressive enough. More significantly, however, Gruda appears particularly well suited to the type of football Klopp wants Germany to play.

Sources indicate that wirtz entered November in a somewhat different position from Gruda. The Liverpool playmaker had already established himself as one of Germany’s most influential performers under Klopp, even if his difficult adjustment to English football continued to attract considerable scrutiny.

GGFN previously examined whether Wirtz could translate his increasingly impressive Germany performances into greater success at Liverpool. That question remains pertinent, but his progress at international level has become difficult to dispute.

It has been revealed that indeed, the most notable development may be the clarity with which Klopp now appears to understand how best to deploy him. The 4-1-4-1 used in November positioned him ahead of Kimmich, alongside Pavlovic, and permitted the Liverpool professional to influence Germany’s attacking play between the opposition’s midfield and defensive lines.

Against Serbia, Wirtz constantly involved himself in the short-passing combinations that helped the Germans establish control. His quick reactions and composed finish supplied Germany’s second goal after Kai Havertz’s initial attempt was saved. The Liverpool playmaker was also active in the counterpress, frequently responding to turnovers by immediately attempting to regain possession.

The Netherlands encounter provided an even more emphatic demonstration of his abilities. Wirtz’s first goal in the 60th minute resulted directly from his aggressive work without the ball.

Recent findings suggest that after exchanging passes with Scherhant near the Dutch penalty area, the German attacking midfielder initially lost possession when Denzel Dumfries intervened. Wirtz nevertheless persisted, recovered the ball himself, and manipulated his way into shooting space before dispatching an outstanding left-footed finish into the corner.

Recent findings suggest that eleven minutes later, he produced another superb attacking contribution. Wirtz initiated the sequence himself by distributing the ball to Gruda on the right. Rather than remaining in his original position, he continued his run toward the penalty area, where Gruda eventually found him with a precise square pass.

The first-time finish beneath the crossbar completed his brace.

Three goals across two matches. Four in total since Klopp assumed responsibility for the national team.

At this stage, one can reasonably argue that the Liverpool professional has become the most notable creative reference point in Germany’s emerging attacking system.

Recent findings suggest that what a remarkable month for the Berlin native! Scherhant already numbered among the more successful newcomers from Klopp’s first international window. He retained his place when the Bundestrainer reduced his original selection and entered November hoping to build upon two promising Germany starts.

It has been revealed that his display against Serbia was encouraging without being spectacular. Three days later, however, the 24-year-old produced an unforgettable display in his hometown. As Get German Football News documented in its feature on Scherhant’s emotional Berlin homecoming, the former Hertha BSC youngster had arranged approximately 50 tickets for family members and friends ahead of Monday’s encounter.

He certainly gave them their money’s worth.

Sources indicate that scherhant attacked the Dutch defence with pace and conviction from the opening stages, frequently seeking individual duels and attempting to manufacture shooting opportunities. His first major chance came in the 32nd minute, when a delivery from Freiburg teammate Philipp Treu reached him near the edge of the penalty area. Scherhant turned and struck the outside of the post.

Nine minutes later, Kimmich supplied him with possession in a dangerous area. Scherhant cut inside and unleashed a magnificent effort into the upper-right corner. The opening goal set Germany on their way to victory and represented a particularly emotional moment for a player who had spent much of his youth dreaming of becoming a professional footballer in Berlin.

Scherhant nearly added another goal immediately after the restart and subsequently contributed to Germany’s fifth by striking the post before Gruda converted the rebound.

The winger’s rise becomes even more remarkable when placed in the context of his career.

Industry observers note that GGFN’s October feature on Scherhant’s unconventional journey to the national team documented the difficulties he encountered at several Berlin clubs before eventually establishing himself at Hertha. His subsequent move to Freiburg has proved especially key.

In a recent development, scherhant’s excellent technical qualities are now being supplemented by the work rate and defensive commitment Klopp demands from his wide attackers. The Bundestrainer explicitly praised the enormous amount of running and defensive work performed by Scherhant and Gruda against the Netherlands. A player once deemed unlikely to progress beyond the Regionalliga now appears capable of securing a lasting place in the German national team.

The captain’s inclusion may initially appear somewhat peculiar. After all, Kimmich hardly required the November international break to establish himself as one of Germany’s most accomplished footballers. The skipper’s position within Klopp’s emerging midfield structure had become the subject of considerable discussion.

Recent findings suggest that the Bayern midfielder sat out Germany’s October victory over Serbia as the Bundestrainer continued experimenting with younger alternatives. Aleksandar Pavlovic, Tom Bischof, and Florian Wirtz combined particularly well in his absence, immediately prompting questions about whether Germany might function more effectively without their established captain.

Get German Football News examined the debate over Kimmich’s role, noting both Klopp’s desire to experiment and his insistence that the Bayern veteran remained an important part of his looks. November provided a footballing answer. Kimmich returned to the starting XI against Serbia and occupied the solitary holding midfield position in Germany’s 4-1-4-1.

The role suited him rather well.

Recent findings suggest that while Pavlovic advanced into the interior spaces, Kimmich assumed responsibility for distributing possession from deeper positions and maintaining the team’s passing rhythm. The captain supplied several useful forward deliveries during the first half and released Gruda for his spectacular solo goal after the interval. His distribution and positional intelligence contributed significantly to Germany’s control of the match.

Industry observers note that an even better performance followed against the Netherlands. Kimmich supplied the opening pass in the sequence that produced Germany’s first meaningful opportunity, repeatedly identified passing lanes into advanced areas, and set up Scherhant’s opening goal. His intelligent distribution continued after the restart, while another pass into Scherhant initiated the sequence that eventually produced Gruda’s fifth goal.

Perhaps the most significant tactical development concerns the relationship between Kimmich and Pavlovic.

Sources indicate that the latter had operated as Germany’s principal holding midfielder during the previous international window. November demonstrated that the two Bayern professionals can function effectively together without requiring either to replicate the other’s preferred responsibilities.

Sources indicate that the international break established that Kimmich remains more than capable of directing the tempo of Klopp’s Germany from central midfield. The captain will surely appreciate having demonstrated that on the pitch.

Industry observers note that schlotterbeck’s inclusion among the winners requires a slightly different explanation. Unlike most of the players discussed thus far, the Borussia Dortmund centre-back did not start both matches. Indeed, he spent the entirety of Germany’s victory in Belgrade on the bench.

Industry observers note that klopp preferred Newcastle United defender Malick Thiaw alongside Jonathan Tah against Serbia, reportedly valuing Thiaw’s aerial qualities in a matchup that called for considerable physical presence. Schlotterbeck nevertheless returned to the starting XI against the Netherlands.

It has been revealed that his performance justified the decision emphatically. The Dortmund professional established himself as an key part of Germany’s defensive structure from the opening stages. Schlotterbeck’s distribution also added something useful to Germany’s buildup.

The defender’s most key contribution arrived in the 64th minute. With the Netherlands attempting to construct an attack from the back, Schlotterbeck advanced aggressively to pressure the opposition’s buildup. His movement forced the Dutch into difficulties, enabling Scherhant to recover possession and draw a foul.

Gruda delivered the resulting free kick. Schlotterbeck attacked the delivery and guided a precise header into the corner, scoring Germany’s third goal and effectively putting the result beyond doubt. Schlotterbeck’s second goal for country could not have arrived at a better time.

The combination of pressing work and attacking contribution represented an excellent illustration of Klopp’s demands. Schlotterbeck wasn’t finished defensively either. In the 70th minute, the Dortmund man made an notable intervention against a dangerous Dumfries delivery, clearing the ball while falling to the ground.

According to recent reports, the performance in Berlin offered a powerful argument for restoring Schlotterbeck to a more permanent role alongside Tah. The partnership combined physical reliability with progressive passing, while Schlotterbeck’s willingness to advance into the opposition half suited Germany’s aggressive pressing approach.

Schlotterbeck took emphatic advantage of his opportunity.

Pavlovic turned in two excellent performances. Pavlovic occupied an key position within Germany’s midfield structure during Klopp’s October assignments, most notably when he combined with Tom Bischof and Florian Wirtz during the 2-0 victory over Serbia.

Industry observers note that as GGFN documented in its earlier tactical examination of Klopp’s midfield, Pavlovic’s composure in possession and willingness to circulate the ball under pressure helped Germany establish a more coherent attacking structure. The obvious question entering November was how the youngster would adapt to the return of Joshua Kimmich.

The answer proved encouraging. Rather than displacing Pavlovic, Klopp retained the midfielder in his starting XI and adjusted his responsibilities. Kimmich took over as the solitary holding midfielder in the 4-1-4-1, while Pavlovic pushed into the more advanced central midfield line alongside Wirtz.

The arrangement presented an interesting challenge for a footballer more accustomed to functioning as one of the deepest players in his team’s possession structure. Pavlovic nevertheless adapted well.

Against Serbia, the midfielder was particularly effective in helping Germany establish control during the opening half. His most significant attacking contribution came in the 14th minute, when he reacted to a Serbian turnover by releasing Havertz with an excellent forward pass. The Arsenal striker’s initial effort was saved, but Wirtz converted the rebound to give Germany a two-goal advantage.

According to recent reports, the pass illustrated Pavlovic’s capacity to influence the attacking game from a more advanced starting position. Pavlovic retained his place against the Netherlands and again operated ahead of his Bayern teammate.

Sources indicate that the opening half wasn’t entirely convincing, but the  youngster improved considerably after the interval. His passing became more assured, and he contributed more actively to Germany’s increasingly dominant possession phases. Pavlovic also advanced into a shooting position in the 74th minute, forcing Dutch goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen into a save.

It has been revealed that the significance of these two appearances lies in the options they provide Klopp. Get German Football News previously examined Pavlovic’s growing importance within Bayern’s midfield, where his established relationship with Kimmich has helped both players develop a strong understanding.

That connection may prove particularly valuable at international level.

The final place goes to a footballer who has quietly become one of the most important beneficiaries of Klopp’s willingness to introduce unfamiliar faces into the national team. GGFN examined Treu’s ambitions to establish himself at right-back when he received his first senior nomination in September. At that stage, the Freiburg professional represented an intriguing alternative for a position at which Germany had struggled to establish continuity.

In a recent development, two months later, Treu has accumulated further international experience and appears increasingly comfortable with the demands placed upon him. The 25-year-old retained his position for both November fixtures. Against Serbia, Treu frequently moved infield from right-back to support Germany’s combinations in central areas. His aggressive defensive approach and willingness to push forward reflected Klopp’s instructions.

In a recent development, the Netherlands match presented considerably greater challenges. Treu was not entirely secure defensively during the opening stages. Cody Gakpo escaped him before delivering a dangerous cross toward Donyell Malen in the 26th minute, demonstrating that the Freiburg man still has areas of his game to refine.

Sources indicate that nevertheless, Treu remained an key attacking outlet. He was continuously available on the right and supplied the delivery from which Scherhant struck the post in the 32nd minute. The move itself offered an excellent example of Germany’s attacking cooperation. Kimmich initiated the sequence from midfield, finding Gruda on the right. The Leipzig attacker moved the ball on to Treu, whose delivery located Scherhant in a dangerous central position.

In a recent development, treu’s inclusion is therefore not necessarily a reward for two spectacular individual performances. Rather, the Freiburg defender emerges as a winner because of the key position he now occupies in Klopp’s squad hierarchy. The Bundestrainer has continued to trust him, including in an important encounter against the Netherlands, and Treu has responded with disciplined, industrious performances.

Industry observers note that one of the more interesting aspects of Germany’s November international break was the consistency of Klopp’s personnel selections and the more clearly defined structure within which they operated. Having experimented extensively during September and October, the Bundestrainer retained a 4-1-4-1 in both matches, making only two changes to the starting XI between Belgrade and Berlin.

The underlying arrangement was important.

For the Netherlands encounter, Nico Schlotterbeck replaced Thiaw in central defence, while Nathaniel Brown came in for Mittelstädt at left-back.

Industry observers note that as GGFN established in its examination of Klopp’s opening international assignments, the Bundestrainer’s early experimentation involved different midfield partnerships, variable fullback assignments, and frequent changes in the positioning of the wide attackers. November offered a more settled approach, even if the precise relationships between the players continued to change according to the circumstances of each match.

The advantage of the November midfield arrangement concerned the fact that Germany could retain Kimmich’s distribution while allowing Pavlovic to contribute to attacks from more advanced positions. Wirtz was also afforded considerable freedom to move between the lines and connect with the wide attackers.

According to recent reports, havertz frequently dropped away from the highest position to participate in combinations, opening space for midfield runners and creating opportunities for Gruda and Scherhant to move inside. The shape could consequently change considerably during possession without abandoning the 4-1-4-1 as its starting reference.

In a recent development, there is no need to declare Germany’s tactical development complete after two victories. The defensive vulnerabilities evident early against the Netherlands and during Serbia’s stronger second-half spells suggest that the national team still has work to do when opponents escape the initial press. Moreover, the competition for positions remains considerable.

In a recent development, schlotterbeck’s performance has strengthened his claim to a regular place alongside Tah, but Thiaw remains a credible alternative. Pavlovic’s successful adaptation to the advanced midfield role provides another option without diminishing the importance of Bischof and Germany’s other central midfield candidates.

Industry observers note that treu has emerged as a trusted right-back, while Gruda and Scherhant have made powerful arguments for continued selection on the wings. The strongest tactical conclusion concerns the greater coherence of the team’s overall structure. Klopp has moved from experimenting with a remarkably large number of players to establishing a recognizable 4-1-4-1 in which established internationals and emerging talents complement one another.

The high pressing and counterpressing remain important, but the positional relationships in midfield and the improved cooperation between the wide players and fullbacks have given Germany greater attacking variety.

In a recent development, the rewards of that approach were obvious in Berlin. Germany will enter the Nations League quarter-finals next March with renewed confidence, greater tactical clarity, and considerably more competition for places.

The upcoming Bundestrainer has plenty of decisions still to make.

For the first time in quite a while, that feels like a very welcome problem.

It has been revealed that fabrizio Romano, giornalista, si è soffermato sul mercato del Napoli sul suo canale Youtube: “I numeri di Gustavo Varela del Monza sono una sorpresa per tutti, oggi diventa protagonista di mercato in Italia e non solo. In 10 partite ha fatto 9 gol e 1 assist da quando è arrivato in Italia e Varela sta dimostrando di essere all’altezza. Il Monza ha pagato il colpo dal Benfica solo 2 milioni. La squadra che è stata più vicina a Varela è stato il Loxer in Francia, ma i suoi agenti poi l’hanno convinto a trasferirsi al Monza. La valutazione di Varela è sui 30-40 milioni di euro, a queste cifre è difficile trattenerlo. Ad oggi dicono che è impossibile che una squadra lo prenda in prestito al Monza fino alla fine della stagione 35 milioni per accordarsi col Monza, poi il Benfica in 5 giorni potrà pareggiare l’offerta e trattare con il ragazzo. Ad oggi è molto difficile un suo ritorno al Benfica. Il Napoli ha già avuto un incontro con gli agenti di Varela, perché ha ottimi rapporti visto che sono gli stessi di Rafa Marin e Alisson Santos. La Juve per gennaio sta cercando di capire se ha la possibilità di prenderlo a gennaio. In Premier il Tottenham e il Brighton, due club forti anche economicamente, si sono interessati a Varela. La differenza può farla lo stipendio offerto al giocatore”.

£329m spent and still no goals for sorry Tottenham

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tottenham Hotspur have never before in the club’s history begun a league season without scoring a single goal in the first four games, although having done so after spending £329m on new players really does take some doing.

Recent findings suggest that “Please score a goal!” was the homemade sign from two Spurs fans upon which the television cameras lingered at the end of the game, although the jaunty felt-tip design and glued-on team crest were rather upbeat compared to the gloom of the stadium. Spurs have tried to outrun their past but it just keeps catching up with them.

Industry observers note that A team reimagined, a manager freshly rolled out and yet they are back in the same grip of anxiety that accompanied them on two consecutive 17th-place finishes in the last two seasons. By the end of this they might have been glad to escape with a single point against Everton, the one team in the Premier League who closed the window with a net transfer profit.

Industry observers note that for Roberto De Zerbi, there was another passionate defence of his team afterwards. “The people, the fans already understand if I make excuses or not,” he remarked. “I came last season when the s--- was like this”, he gestured to a level somewhere around the midpoint of his forehead. “I have always been… not positive but realistic. I am sorry for the result that it’s not immediately the improvement. We played as a team. We didn’t score. We didn’t win [but] we played as a team.”.

Indeed he co-opted the Italian term “sbloccare” to describe his team’s problem. They simply need to unlock – or unblock – the team and the goals would flow. He joked that in Italy he would be lauded for two consecutive clean sheets in this game and the previous one against Nottingham Forest. “What did you write?” he demanded of one of the Italian newspaper correspondents. “You have the passport.”.

Spurs have one last game at home this month, on Saturday against Aston Villa, to end the streak in September. They were into the second half before the first attempt on target that obliged Jordan Pickford to make a save – Mateus Fernandes’s shot slapping limply against the Everton goalkeeper’s gloves to ironic cheers from the home fans.

At the end De Zerbi could not contain his frustration, unable to wait until he reached the privacy of the dressing room to tell Mathys Tel where he had gone wrong. He did so with the Spurs substitute still wiping the sweat from his brow on the pitch. The player did not look at all impressed. De Zerbi mentioned later that he was simply reminding his player of what it took to play as a central striker.

It has been revealed that “There is a term in Italian, ‘sbloccare’ that literally translates as ‘unblock’… I know we can score goals and win games. We have to respect the history of the players – if you forget [Dominic] Solanke and [Omar] Marmoush the others haven’t scored many in their careers. I think we can find the goals with the quality of the players.”.

Spurs play Liverpool at Anfield in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday before Villa a week today. The Spurs record at home is dismal. In the last 35 games they have won just five, drawn 10 and lost a remarkable 20. This new stadium has become a problem for the team in it – or maybe it is the other way around.

A good result for Everton, who were under pressure for most of the first half but had much the better of it after the break. David Moyes’s team finished the game with more shots on target than the home team. Moyes managed the game well and trusted his team to withstand the Spurs possession in the first half until they reached a point where Everton could start to push back.

According to recent reports, hard to pick out any major chances – it was that kind of game – but Brennan Johnson should have won it for the away team in the second half. The ball was cut back to him by Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and the former Spurs man skied his shot.

Sources indicate that some surprised faces then when Moyes stated later that he had expected a lot more from his team. He acknowledged the resilience in defence and the importance of the clean sheet. “We played well enough,” he said, “but when we had the ball we turned it over more often than we should have done.”.

The game had started with Vitaliy Mykolenko being tortured by the pace of Sávio and ended with the Ukrainian left-back being given the man of the match award. Like many of his team-mates, he had hung in there. There was another fine performance from Jarrad Branthwaite at centre-half and Moyes said that he hoped it might earn him a place in the England squad. “He is still finding his way back from injury,” Moyes said, “it would be great if he could get a call-up.”.

Industry observers note that in the directors’ box were the usual pained expressions of Vinai Venkatesham, the Spurs chief executive, and chairman Peter Charrington. They sat alongside Vivienne Lewis, daughter of the patriarch Joe. There is a certain fatigue about the home crowd when faced with afternoons like this which suggests they have seen so much that the bar is quite high – or low – to provoke a really splenetic response. Perhaps it is just too early in the season although the final whistle was met with boos.

The first shot on target of the entire game for either side was a free-kick struck by James Garner in added time at the end of the first half. Spurs had started at a ferocious pace although they could not sustain it.

It has been revealed that de Zerbi complained about the pre-season injuries on tour in Australia and also the lack of time he had to integrate Sávio and Marmoush. He mentioned that his team were not in the right “physical condition”.

“We played very well in the first 30 minutes and maybe the energy and the fact we didn’t score – we lost confidence.” By the end, he had sent on James Maddison, Tel, Lucas Bergvall and Mohammed Kudus to little avail. Everton looked more likely to win it.

Recent findings suggest that speaking to Sky Sports, the Everton defender remarked: “You look at the game from the start, they put us under pressure and we had to dig deep to stay in the game. Then we grew into the game towards the end of the first half and showed that mentality again in the second half.

Recent findings suggest that “We had chances to win the game as well. The backs to the wall mentality will help us go a long way. If we can keep clean sheets, you can go a long way in the league. But it’s not just us the defenders. It’s the whole team working hard. It’s a team effort.”.

"I feel like we could've taken three points" James Tarkowski speaks after his sides draw with Spurs 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/Wdj3N5hk8l.

Recent findings suggest that "Six hours and we've not scored a goal? It's a DISGRACE" 😬Ashley Young claims that the Spurs players will need to have conversations about their lack of threat going forward ❌ pic.twitter.com/0KNomGEavx.

"Absolutely diabolical" 😬Jamie Redknapp on Spurs not scoring in their first four Premier League games 😳 pic.twitter.com/48Nbxymlev.

It has been revealed that tottenham failed to take the attacking initiative or create any notable chances. De Zerbi used multiple forward players in a host of attacking positions, but no one could find the breakthrough.

Sources indicate that boos ring around the ground as Spurs and Everton both have to settle for a point. Tottenham’s winless start to the season continues, while Everton’s unbeaten run remains intact. Spurs haven’t managed a goal in six hours of Premier League football across the 2026-27 campaign. Tottenham sit 17th with two points. Everton are up to seventh and will certainly take the draw.

FULL-TIME: The points are shared between Spurs and Everton at Tottenham Hotspur stadium 🤝 pic.twitter.com/HwPuKI3Ajh.

Sources indicate that dewsbury-Hall’s deflected effort flies out for a corner. Everton can’t make the most of the resulting set piece and Tottenham survive.

There will be three minutes of added time. Are we set for late drama at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium?

Recent findings suggest that pickford makes an error as his poor clearance is intercepted by Maddison. The ball is eventually worked to Bergvall, whose curling effort is parried away by the Everton goalkeeper.

According to recent reports, jordan Pickford gets down well to deny Lucas Bergvall! 🧤 pic.twitter.com/59uoHTqto6.

It has been revealed that tosin comes on for his Spurs debut as he replaces Gray. Can anyone be Tottenham’s hero and find a late winner?

Sources indicate that garner is booked after he clatters into Savio. Everton have produced a tough and disciplined defensive perfomance so far.

Spurs are now enjoying a sustained period of possession. They’re waiting to fashion a big chance and end their wait for a top-flight goal in the 2026-27 season.

Sources indicate that de Zerbi makes another change as Maddison enters the action with applause from the Spurs faithful. He replaces Marmoush. It looks like Tel is now operating as a false nine.

Industry observers note that johnson misses a huge chance! Dewsbury-Hall fires a low cross into his path and Johnson takes the chance with a first-time shot, but he slices his effort and it goes over the bar. He’s got to do better from that range inside the penalty area.

That opportunity is Johnson’s last action of the match as he comes off for Hackney. O’Brien is also introduced, replacing Maitland-Niles.

Industry observers note that that was the chance. Dewsbury-Hall rolls it into the path of Spurs’ Europa League final winner Brennan Johnson and he skied it. He hasn’t scored since he left Spurs in January for Palace.

According to recent reports, everton look like the far likelier side to break the deadlock. De Zerbi’s changes have done little to affect the game. Marmoush is cutting a very frustrated figure up top for Spurs.

Industry observers note that bergvall finds Savio with a whipped cross. The winger tries to help the ball back into the danger zone, but Pickford reacts quickly and collects possession.

Dewsbury-Hall picks up the game’s first yellow card after catching Tonali with a late sliding challenge.

What is Kinsky doing?! The goalkeeper’s dreadful pass which was intended for Tonali is intercepted by Dewsbury-Hall, who tries to slide a low effort through Kinsky’s legs. The Tottenham man redeems himself with a crucial save to keep the scoreline goalless. The hosts are living so dangerously. Kinsky needs to wake up.

Moyes responds with a straight swap on the wing as Grealish comes on for George.

Industry observers note that enter: Grealish. He is on for Tyrique George. Surprised that Brennan Johnson survived that change. He has struggled to make an impression.

Following Spurs’ reshuffle, it looks like Savio will stay out wide on the right, with Tel on the left. Kudus will sit as the central playmaker behind Marmoush, who is now the lone frontman.

De Zerbi orders a much-needed triple change as Kudus, Tel and Bergvall replace Solanke, Fernandes and Bentancur.

Jack Grealish has long since stopped the warm-up on the touchline and is now just staring at the game in expectation of his introduction.

A couple of chances for Everton. Spurs have survived but they look so vulnerable when Everton turn over possession. Crowd could turn soon. Almost reached the hour-mark on matchday 4 and still no Spurs’ Premier League goal.

The start of Spurs’ second-half performance is alarmingly similar to their display against Newcastle two weeks ago. That day, Tottenham allowed Newcastle to seize the initiative and they netted two second-half goals without reply. Everton are gaining confidence as Spurs continue to lack courage or threat. The crowd is getting more and more restless.

Industry observers note that tottenham fail to clear a corner and the ball lands at George’s feet. The Everton winger shoots but his fierce drive is blocked by Bentancur. The whole of Spurs’ bench is warming up. The visitors presently have the momentum and the hosts look nervous.

Everton are looking threatening once again as George attempts to thread a pass through to Johnson on the counter-attack, but Van de Ven is there to clear.

It has been revealed that george does brilliantly to escape away from Gray and floats a cross towards the back post. Barry rises highest and his close-range header is blocked by Kinsky. The Tottenham goalkeeper didn’t know much about it, but that’s a massive stop. Undoubtedly the game’s most dangerous moment in front of goal so far.

Spurs’ first shot has arrived! Unfortunately, Fernandes’ tame long-range effort is easily gathered by Pickford. There were some sarcastic cheers from the Tottenham fans as Fernandes took aim. They clearly want more attacking inspiration from their players.

According to recent reports, ironic cheers as Spurs have their first shot on target. It has taken them until the start of the second half and it would be hard to say Fernandes stung the palms of Pickford.

It has been revealed that we are back under way for the second half. Everton and Spurs are both unchanged at the break. With the anxiety building in the stadium as the game remains goalless, how long will De Zerbi wait before making a change?

It has been revealed that an uneventful first half of football comes to a close. In a game lacking rhythm, creativity and attacking spark, nothing separates Tottenham and Everton at the break. Spurs’ search for a first Premier League goal this season continues.

According to recent reports, there will be two added minutes. Everton have a free kick on the edge of Spurs’ penalty area. Garner and Dewsbury-Hall are standing over it. The former Manchester United and Nottingham Forest midfielder takes it and his effort bounces in front of Kinsky, who pushes it out for a corner.

James Garner free-kick pushed away by Kinsky is the game’s first attempt on target.

There has not been a single attempt on target at 40:27 from either team. Spurs have had the best of it but even so. That’s a poor return.

Another attack fizzles out for Spurs. Substitute Jack Grealish engaging in some badinage with home fans as he warms up. He famously agreed a move to Spurs in 2018, called off at the eleventh hour when Aston Villa were sold to the current ownership.

In a recent development, that is so poor from Fernandes. The summer signing’s overhit corner drifts out for a goal kick. Suddenly, Spurs’ attacking play has fallen quite flat.

Pickford does well to intercept Robertson’s inviting low cross. The left back needed Solanke or Marmoush to make a darting near-post run there to give him more options.

Spurs are bossing this game but on the rare occasions Everton escape you do wonder if they might score.

It has been revealed that tottenham are roared on by the home support to move the ball a bit quicker going forward. Out of possession, Everton almost revert to a back five, with Garner dropping very deep near to Tarkowski and Branthwaite.

Tonali picks out Gray with a pinpoint pass. Garner is alert to the danger and tracks back to clear, stopping Gray from getting a one-on-one opportunity.

It has been revealed that maitland-Niles does very well to dispossess Tonali in a dangerous area, allowing Barry to tee up Dewsbury-Hall, but his shot is smothered by the Spurs defence. Mykolenko then chips a cross into a box, but it’s tapped behind for a corner by Robertson. Moyes will certainly be encouraged by this side’s resurgence over the last 10 minutes.

There is a break in play here with Gray down and receiving treatment after a collision. He appears to be holding his lower back. The Tottenham man gingerly gets back to his feet and trudges off the pitch.

According to recent reports, gray down for some extended treatment. Richarlison in the stands. Spurs in danger of losing early momentum.

After Spurs’ fast start, Everton have grown into the contest over the last five minutes and are getting on the ball far higher up the pitch.

Garner’s corner is cleared by Spurs, but only as far as Maitland-Niles. In similar range to where he scored that stunning equaliser against Manchester United, the former Arsenal man shoots, but his attempt fizzes well wide.

Sources indicate that spurs are really flowing here. Finding the balls through the lines and real speed when they attack Everton. Major question is whether they can convert that into goals. Van Hecke and Fernandes both had chances.

Sávio has had a fine start to the game. Mykolenko in for a long afternoon. Spurs have looked dangerous and should be 1-0 up.

Tonali finds Savio with a deep cross, leaving Pickford in no-man’s land. The Brazilian keeps the ball in play and it loops up, just out of Marmoush’s reach.

Robertson floats a teasing delivery into Van Hecke at the back post, but the centre-back directs his half-volley over the bar from close range.

In a recent development, spurs then burst forward again through Savio, who feeds Fernandes. The playmaker’s low drive is heroically blocked by Tarkowski as Everton continue to hold on (just about).

Industry observers note that as expected, it’s Tottenham with all the early possession, with Everton sitting very deep and soaking up the early pressure. Marmoush turns Armstrong and wins a free-kick in a dangerous area.

They’re under way in north London, the hosts are in their lily-white and navy kit, with Everton in their grey/dirty green (is that a colour?!) away number.

In a recent development, greetings from N17. It’s a wonderful, warm late summer evening. As expected there is the usual foreboding from the home fans. Two defeats and one draw. The mood will sour further if Spurs do not win today. No Porro or Udogie so Archie Gray, ever adaptable, starts at right-back again.

Everton are undefeated with five points from three games. They have a decent 16/17 players but it is the reserves beyond that which everyone is concerned about. Grealish and Dibling on the bench give them two potential game-changers. Spurs’ squad looks very strong on the team-sheet. A full bench of experienced pros and no fillers. On the pitch it has been less convincing.

Brennan Johnson spent two years at Tottenham and scored the winning goal in the 1-0 Europa League final victory over Manchester United in May 2025, ending the club’s 17-year trophy drought.

After a short, disappointing spell at Crystal Palace, Johnson joined Everton last month, with Dwight McNeil moving in the opposite direction.

Recent findings suggest that the Welsh winger starts for Everton today. Could he hurt his previous employers on a day where they desperately need a win?

Recent findings suggest that brennan in the building. 💙 pic.twitter.com/94GgAY8c56.

Midfielder took exception to negativity surrounding club after moves for players on deadline day failed to materialise.

Industry observers note that “We signed Jack [Grealish], which was nice, and I’d been speaking to him,” says Dewsbury-Hall, sitting in a café at the club’s Finch Farm training base. “But I had seen all the stuff [online], all the meltdowns about this and that and, in all honestly, it annoyed me a bit.

Recent findings suggest that “I get where people are coming from. Everyone wants to sign everyone and have the perfect squad, but there are still 19 lads in this building who are going to hopefully take this club to good things this year. That was getting disregarded. I was seeing people saying: ‘We’ll be lucky to stay up this year.’.

“What message is that sending to the lads who are already here? I’m not blaming anyone. We get it. It didn’t work. But let’s all be positive – right, it’s done, bang, let’s go. That’s what we’ve been trying to say in the dressing room.”.

Earlier this week, Mykhailo Mudryk picked up an ankle injury in training which has ruled the Chelsea loanee out of action for as long as two months.

The winger only made his debut for Tottenham as a late substitute against Nottingham Forest last week, but his attempt to rebuild his career following his anti-doping ban has been dealt a major blow.

Folarin Balogun’s proposed £39m move from Monaco collapsed on transfer deadline day, Richarlison’s return to the club didn’t materialise and Beto was sold to Fiorentina, leaving Thierno Barry as Everton’s only recognised striker.

Nottingham Forest’s pursuit of academy product Harrison Armstrong ruffled the fans’ feathers, while Iliman Ndiaye was sold to Manchester City for £60m.

Dwight McNeil, Tim Iroegbunam, Nathan Patterson, Adam Aznou and Idrissa Gueye were also allowed to leave.

Merlin Rohl and Tyrique George made their loans permanent, while Brennan Johnson, Hayden Hackney and Christian Norgaard were also added to the squad.

Summer signing Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Vitaliy Mykolenko are David Moyes’ only options at full-back.

Overall, there were a number of solid additions, just not enough of them to cover all the departures.

🎧🫡 Thierno Barry ahead of today's clash in North London. pic.twitter.com/mwlsKH8Pid.

Subs: Dubravka, Tosin, Senesi, Gallagher, Maddison, Tel, Bergvall, Kudus, Davies.

Everton: Pickford; Maitland-Niles, Tarkowski, Brathwaite, Mykolenko; Armstrong, Garner; Johnson, Dewsbury-Hall, George; Barry.

Subs: Travers, O’Brien, Keane, King, Alcaraz, Graham, Hackney, Dibling, Grealish.

After scoring that last-minute leveller against Manchester United last time out, Ainsley Maitland-Niles is promoted to the starting 11 and replaces Merlin Rohl. Brennan Johnson returns to his former club and starts, while Jack Grealish is on the bench.

Today's Toffees to face @SpursOfficial. COYB! ✊#TOTEVE pic.twitter.com/mOcCayRUfm.

Roberto De Zerbi has made four alterations from last weekend’s stalemate with Nottingham Forest. Dominic Solanke, Mateus Fernandes, Archie Gray and Andy Robertson all come into the line-up. Pedro Porro and Destiny Udogie are out injured, while Conor Gallagher and Mathys Tel are relegated to the bench. Tosin Adarabioyo and James Maddison are also among the substitutes.

Our Spurs side to take on Everton 👊🔢 @krakenfx pic.twitter.com/n637s7swiD.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League meeting between Tottenham and Everton in the capital.

According to recent reports, are Tottenham in must-win territory already? It may seem reactionary and premature, but after spending £380m in the summer to revamp an underperforming squad, Tottenham sit inside the relegation zone, with just one point and zero goals scored in three games.

Roberto De Zerbi’s men opened the 2026-27 top-flight season with worrying back-to-back defeats to Brentford and Newcastle United, before ending their losing streak last weekend thanks to a goalless draw against Nottingham Forest.

This game gives Tottenham another opportunity to reverse their dreadful home form. Last season, Spurs managed just three league wins at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and lost 10. The recent 2-0 loss against Newcastle was a painful reminder of Spurs’ shortcomings at home, but they’ll be expected to be authoritative and seize the initiative here today. A much-needed three points would be the perfect remedy to ease the pressure and unwanted attention on De Zerbi and his squad.

In a recent development, meanwhile, Everton have made an unbeaten start to the season, accumulating five points from their first three league matches. David Moyes’ side looked set for defeat last time out, when they were trailing Manchester United 2-1 at the Hill Dickinson Stadium heading into stoppage time, until Ainsley Maitland-Niles’ stunning 96th-minute equaliser salvaged a draw.

Alongside drama on the pitch, there has also been noise off it. A bizarre transfer window has left Everton with a serious lack of depth up top and in both full-back positions. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall responded to the fans’ negativity over this situation, saying their meltdowns “annoyed” him.

Nevertheless, they arrive in North London with all eyes on Tottenham and if the hosts can find a first league victory this season.

Kick-off is at 17:30, with team news coming shortly.

Former Old Firm rivals reveal how clubs walked a fine line between rivalry and respect...and even stopped by for tea and sympathy in times of trouble!

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1355 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:20 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 12:29 EST, 13 November 2026.
  • In a recent development, they have reached an age when they would once have been categorised as the old infirm.
  • They have reached the age when they can reflect on being stalwarts of the Old Firm.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 12:20 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 12:29 EST, 13 November 2026.

In a recent development, they have reached an age when they would once have been categorised as the old infirm. Yet in the autumn of 2026 they cavort around Toryglen with an almost juvenile vigour.

They have reached the age when they can reflect on being stalwarts of the Old Firm. Yet they are outlining prepares and strategy for a vital, growing movement.

The two meetings are separated by two sets of stairs. On the ground level, men of pensionable age and beyond play walking football. Just above sit Campbell Ogilvie, former secretary of Rangers and president of the Scottish FA, and Eric Riley, once firm secretary and director of Celtic.

They are both on the board of Walking Football Scotland, an organisation that now has more than 5,000 people playing the game across 160 clubs, with participants ranging from 40 to 93.

The venerable statesmen of the Scottish game may be perceived to be rivals, but only in matters on the pitch. They sit in an office in the south side of Glasgow and reminisce about how they first met 50 years ago when playing five-a-sides and then renewed that rivalry in their professional life.

As the Glasgow rivals now seem regularly at odds, both men recalled a time when friendship was paramount amid the sporting mayhem.

Former Rangers secretary Campbell Ogilvie and ex-Celtic director Eric Riley are firm friends.

‘The two clubs always had a good relationship back in those days,’ stated Ogilvie, now 76 and still playing football. ‘We wanted to beat each other — naturally. But off the field we had a very close relationship.’.

He told a remarkable story that backs that assertion.

According to recent reports, ‘There was one day I was at Ibrox in the early 1980s when the team was not doing so well. The phone rang and it was Sean Fallon, Jock Stein’s former Celtic assistant. I had known Sean from my days with the Scottish League and he stated: “I know you’re going through a rocky spell, so I’m coming over for a cup of tea”.

‘Over he comes. So there was a very close relationship in those days. I’m not there now and for all I know there still is. But certainly, when I was there and Eric was at Celtic, we could talk to each other.’.

Riley, 69, agreed: ‘Absolutely. John McClelland (former Rangers chairman) was one we could talk to. And Martin (Bain, former chief executive) I suppose, when he came along a bit later. Between myself and Peter Lawwell (former Celtic chief executive and chairman) the relationship between the clubs off the field was actually quite strong. But on the field we still wanted to win.’.

Ogilvie added: ‘There was a respect. And I go back to the Willie Waddells and the Willie Thorntons, there was that respect. More recently that was there with the likes of Jack McGinn and so on.

‘We had a good relationship but it’s fair to say that there was no social media in those days. You know all the toxic stuff that can bring.’.

Sources indicate that the traits of respect and sporting competitiveness have been obvious in both men since they first met half a century ago. ‘We played five-a-side football at Scotstoun before the football careers started. It was just casual games,’ mentioned Ogilvie. ‘We were in our early 20s. Eric was an accountant and I think those games were arranged through accountants.

‘I played youth football when I was 16 and, 60 years down the line, playing football is still a major part of my life.’.

It has been revealed that ogilvie began walking football eight years ago and Riley soon after. ‘I suffer from Parkinson’s, amongst other things,’ noted Riley. ‘I was getting assistance through Stobhill Hospital and the physiotherapist there, who specialises in Parkinson’s patients, got in touch to say there was a project going on at Toryglen where they were playing walking football and assessing you to see what the benefits may or may not be.’.

Ogilvie and Riley are both on the board of Walking Football and have played a substantial role in its rise.

Recent findings suggest that riley agreed to take part. ‘I really enjoyed it because you are back playing football again, you have the camaraderie and you have the home baking which I never really get at home.’.

In a recent development, riley had a hip replacement in March and admitted: ‘I have not played since then. I miss it. I play a few other things which are more and more difficult. I play tennis.’.

According to recent reports, his tennis history is illustrious as he played with Judy Murray in Scottish championships. ‘She went off to the tour and I went off to university,’ notes Riley. He is unstinting in his praise of the woman who became the mother of the No1 in men’s singles and men’s doubles.

In a recent development, the repartee between Riley and Ogilvie is relaxed but both men have a resolve to grow walking football. Their task has been helped by bookmakers William Hill stepping in with sponsorship.

According to recent reports, the benefits of the sport stretch beyond the physical. Ogilvie gave his own experience.

‘When you have finished working, there is a void, not mixing with people, not being with people, and walking football certainly has helped me fill that. Hopefully it helps me keep a bit fitter too,’ he remarked.

Ogilvie pointed out: ‘The concerns you tend to encounter are health. Grief is another one. There are quite a few of the guys who have lost their wives and quite a few who are just sitting on the sofa watching Homes Under the Hammer.’.

Walking football, too, has attracted a large cadre of women. ‘One of the things that stood out for me was the number of females playing,’ stated Riley. ‘I went along to my first session and there were four female players, three of whom had never kicked a football in their life previously. Walking football got them involved and they really enjoyed it.’.

Walking football has made giant leaps in Scotland but the next step is to collate data so cases for funding will be made unanswerable.

Industry observers note that ‘We need facts or what is called data,’ said Ogilvie. ‘We are trying to do some studies with universities to get that data — physical and mental — and get it to the government. We want to prove the benefits and then we could make this prescriptive through surgeries.

‘We see the benefits day to day anecdotally but that doesn’t bring you the data. Sponsorship helps.

Walking Football attracts thousands of participants at clubs across the country.

‘The university studies won’t come overnight because they need to be detailed. But if we could get to the stage where we could prove the benefits, then the NHS and the government would see that proof in black and white.’.

This is all serious and proper. But both men were keen to emphasise that the game was fun. Ogilvie noted: ‘When I started, I asked someone: “How would you sum up walking football?” He said to me: “It’s a cross between watching Barcelona and the Gurkha warriors”.’.

He added: ‘I loved when at the end of an over-75s tournament one player noted to another: “Good game, son”.’.

In a recent development, the football world has thus moved into a new era. But some things cannot change. Ogilvie said: ‘One of my grandsons, who is 10, came along to watch a session and said two things. Firstly, it is a bit more intense than he thought and second there are no pink boots.’.

Riley chimed in: ‘That would be an affront, that would be unacceptable.’.

Even in walking football some things are a step too far.

Industry observers note that ■ Eric Riley and Campbell Ogilvie were speaking at the announcement of William Hill as official sponsor of Walking Football Scotland. To find your nearest game visit walkingfootballscotland.org.

Così Carlo Ancelotti ha risposto alle critiche dell'ex attaccante brasiliano, che domenica aveva chiesto pubblicamente il suo esonero dopo la sconfitta per 3-2 contro il Giappone. "È libertà di espressione e, in un Paese democratico, tutti possono avere un'opinione", ha aggiunto in conferenza stampa l'italiano. In un messaggio pubblicato domenica sui social, Romario aveva scritto: "Ancelotti, è finita! Prendi le tue cose e vattene", sollecitando il presidente della Cbf, Samir Xaud, a prendere una decisione. In a recent development, dobbiamo tornare a essere competitivi. È da molto tempo che non lo siamo", ha dichiarato. Il tecnico ha difeso la fase di sperimentazione e rinnovamento della squadra, spiegando che lo staff sta valutando nuovi giocatori. Ha tuttavia ammesso che contro il Giappone sono emerse carenze soprattutto in fase difensiva. "Tutti crediamo che la squadra sia sulla strada giusta e affronteremo Singapore con fiducia", ha aggiunto. 💡 Key Takeaways

  • A gennaio ci aspettiamo un attaccante, un difensore centrale e, all'occorrenza, un esterno.
  • In a recent development, E poi ci sono i due colpi di livello che ci aspettiamo.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, sarà un mercato di gennaio davvero movimentato per il Milan. Ci aspettiamo almeno due o tre rinforzi importanti per migliorare la rosa. Ci sono alcuni ruoli che necessitano di aggiustamenti e Ruben Amorim vorrebbe degli elementi in più per gestire le rotazioni senza incidere sulla qualità della squadra.

A gennaio ci aspettiamo un attaccante, un difensore centrale e, all'occorrenza, un esterno. In questo caso potrebbe essere richiamato Athekame dal Lione, ma andrebbe trovato un accordo con la squadra francese per interrompere anticipatamente il prestito che in estate era stato pattuito fino a giugno prossimo. Il giocatore sarebbe felice di ritornare. Sta vivendo il prestito in Francia come un'opportunità per crescere, ma è chiaro che, se dovesse tornare al Milan, sarebbe più che contento.

In a recent development, E poi ci sono i due colpi di livello che ci aspettiamo. Il primo è l'attaccante. Attenzione a Endrick, del Real Madrid. Il brasiliano sta decidendo se lasciare il Real in prestito a gennaio oppure proseguire nella squadra di José Mourinho. Endrick è uno degli obiettivi principali del Milan, probabilmente più di Tresoldi, perché per l'attaccante che gioca al Bruges servono almeno 50-60 milioni di euro.

Sources indicate that con Endrick, invece, si potrebbe impostare anche un'operazione in prestito con diritto di riscatto che diventa obbligo a determinate condizioni. Si può studiare una formula alternativa, anche se la spesa sarebbe comunque importante. Ma Endrick sembra essere proprio uno degli obiettivi principali per l'attacco del Milan, soprattutto per la connessione che c'è tra Roc Nation e RedBird specialmente con la presenza di Yormark, nuovo amministratore delegato della holding Milan Sport Entertainment, che in passato ha lavorato nella Roc Nation e il cui fratello è ancora il CEO dell'azienda che rappresenta giocatori, sportivi e cantanti.

In a recent development, insomma, ci sono i presupposti perché il Milan possa essere uno dei candidati principali per prendere Endrick nel mese di gennaio. La decisione finale, però, spetta al giocatore e al Real Madrid e in queste settimane se ne parlerà in maniera più approfondita, anche in base al minutaggio che avrà il brasiliano a Madrid.

According to recent reports, E poi non ci dimentichiamo del difensore centrale. Sarà sicuramente un giocatore importante, perché già in estate il Milan voleva acquistare un difensore, ma ha sbagliato i tempi ed è arrivato all'ultimo giorno senza riuscire a prenderlo. Tanto che lo stesso Cardinale, in una recente intervista, aveva detto proprio che non era rimasto del tutto soddisfatto degli acquisti fatti in estate: il mercato estivo si poteva fare meglio. E quindi ora, a gennaio, ci sarà modo di riparare a qualche mancanza della scorsa estate.

Sources indicate that il difensore centrale è necessario perché bisogna migliorare le rotazioni. Ci sono problemi in difesa praticamente ogni partita: Pavlovic e De Winter stanno facendo gli straordinari e, se il Milan vuole essere competitivo su più competizioni, deve necessariamente prendere anche un altro difensore centrale.

It has been revealed that attenzione poi anche al centrocampo, perché, se dovesse partire Christian Comotto in prestito, il Milan potrebbe ragionare anche su un altro mediano. Altrimenti i giocatori sarebbero davvero pochi a livello numerico.

Il Milan, con questo mercato di riparazione, potrebbe dare la scossa per la seconda parte della stagione. Ma bisogna stringere i denti ancora per un mese e mezzo, perché dal Frosinone fino al mercato di gennaio ci sono ancora tantissime partite da giocare e da disputare.

Il Milan deve stringere i denti anche con i giocatori infortunati: Saelemaekers, Gabbia e Chukwueze torneranno solamente nel 2027. Dunque, il Milan deve fare affidamento sul materiale che ha a disposizione e sui giocatori che dovranno rientrare presto dall'infermeria per dare una mano. Ruben Amorim, fino a gennaio, dovrà lottare con la squadra che ha a disposizione, in attesa quindi di rinforzi importanti nel mese di gennaio.

Industry observers note that fino ad ora Amorim sta facendo bene, soprattutto in campionato, mentre in Europa League il cammino non è soddisfacente. Nelle prossime due gare di Europa League il Milan dovrà dare un impulso netto alla qualificazione ai playoff, altrimenti sarebbe una grandissima delusione. Ma Amorim è fiducioso perché sta cominciando a vedere il suo vero Milan.

If Spanish refs can speak up so can ours... over to you, Willie

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (593 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:39 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 12:46 EST, 13 November 2026.
  • Since the beginning of the month in Spain, referees have started making themselves available for interview after matches to explain decisions and improve transparency.
  • It has led to people here asking why Scotland’s whistlers aren’t doing the same — and those questions are perfectly valid.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 12:39 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 12:46 EST, 13 November 2026.

Since the beginning of the month in Spain, referees have started making themselves available for interview after matches to explain decisions and improve transparency.

It has led to people here asking why Scotland’s whistlers aren’t doing the same — and those questions are perfectly valid.

Back in August 2023, leading official John Beaton addressed calls for greater openness around VAR and gave the impression the refereeing firmament were in favour of a new spirit of glasnost.

‘Anything to explain how we are arriving at decisions and anything we can do to show people what we do on a Saturday and what happens in the VAR centre, we absolutely welcome,’ he said.

‘The more transparency, the better. The more questions we get, the more answers we can provide and, we hope, get to a better place,’.

Recent findings suggest that that was followed by upcoming head of refereeing Willie Collum’s VAR show on YouTube the following season. At that point, there seemed a real move to lift the lid and build confidence in our men in black. There was talk of Collum doing his programme more than once a month and suggestions referees might even be open to being interviewed post-match in the right circumstances.

Unfortunately, though, all that has come to nothing and last term — in which controversial decisions had a huge effect on the title race — feels like it could become an obstacle in the way of progress.

Head of Referees Willie Collum should be applauded for speaking up on the SFA VAR show.

It needn’t be, though. There has always been a feeling among referees that being put in front of the cameras carried danger. SFA Ian Maxwell has also spoken about the game being subject to ‘fairly hysterical commentary’ when something bad happens.

The media environment here is nowhere near as febrile as in Spain, though. It has four newspapers dedicated to sport alone. There are countless chat shows on council telly full of talking heads. Ages ago, news bulletins there had lipreaders telling viewers what coaches and players were saying on the park. Jose Mourinho is also back ruffling officials’ feathers at Real Madrid.

Getting Spanish refs to a place where they feel ready to be interviewed has taken time. It has also taken extra cash for them from TV money and it can still go a lot further.

A selected referee will speak to broadcast rights-holders only. And it’s not after every game. Only selected fixtures.

The SFA made real progress a couple of years back in lifting the curtain and should seek to rediscover that momentum — even though it won’t make the key problem of having to improve overall standards go away.

It has been revealed that since last year, the Spanish FA have been broadcasting their own YouTube show ‘Tiempo de Revision’ to address flashpoints. It should be said that it’s inferior to Collum’s broadcast in terms of content.

It replays incidents against a musical backdrop with captions explaining the decisions. There is no in-game audio, no one like Collum putting himself out there.

Although some of his reasoning for substantial calls was a bit suspect last term, that programme remains a platform to build from.

Industry observers note that there is no reason why referees shouldn’t explain their decision-making after games here. Criticism they may or may not receive in the aftermath shouldn’t come into it.

If Spanish whistlers can go public, so can they.

Recent findings suggest that bruno Guimarães cupped his ears and had a plastic cup thrown at him as the abuse came down from the stands. Despite the missiles, the Brazilian wore a look that made it clear he was very much enjoying his first goal in an Arsenal shirt.

It has been revealed that mikel Arteta has laid bare his quirky management techniques so his players are ready for any eventuality. Late meals and making the dressing room hotter are among his tricks, although nothing can prepare a player having 40,000 fans calling you a “sad Geordie b------”.

In a recent development, so it was a sweet moment for Guimarães, even more so after coming just after Sunderland had a penalty saved. Other teams with aspirations of the title dropped points earlier in the day, while Arteta could battle to a win with key players brought back into the team and Guimarães coming off the bench at half-time. Sources indicate that “Everyone knows I had a difficult start through injuries in my short time. But I’m glad to be back and glad to play,” Guimarães said. “I feel very good. It was unbelievable to score a beautiful goal, beautiful moment for me and my family and I am happy.”.

“But I loved the save from David, the way the team reacted, the way we go again and we go against everything, but this should never happen, it’s not fair, and I am sad, very sad, in that sense.”.

Industry observers note that when will Martin Zubimendi start again for Arsenal? Mikel Arteta wants to avoid a repeat of last season, when Zubimendi played more games than anyone in Europe, but it is curious that the Spaniard has not yet started a single match of this campaign. It is one thing to reduce his minutes, and another to turn him into a permanent substitute.

Zubimendi has looked quite good off the bench in recent games but has been behind Myles Lewis-Skelly and Mikel Merino in the battle to partner Declan Rice from the start. And that’s before Bruno Guimaraes, the newly introduced £75m signing, reaches full fitness.

In the thick Naples air in midweek, Declan Rice did what he always does: he kept running. Another start for the Arsenal midfielder, another 90 minutes completed and another performance of constructive passing and destructive defending. For anyone who was worried about Rice’s physical condition, it was an emphatic response.

In a recent development, after that Champions League victory over Napoli, Rice insisted he was ready for another marathon campaign. He made 69 appearances for club and country last season, up from 60 the previous term, and believes that is a sustainable number of games, even for an all-action midfielder such as himself. “I have shown I can do it,” he remarked.

It has been revealed that the key question, though, is not whether Rice can do it, but whether he should do it. There is no doubt that his body eventually began to pay the price for his exertions last year, especially during the World Cup, and it would be reasonable for his managers to worry that his extraordinary workload might one day take a serious toll. This, after all, is a footballer who managed nerve pain in his hamstring throughout the second half of last season.

Regis Le Bris, who made 11 changes for the League Cup win over Hull in midweek, reverts to the starting XI that drew at Brentford seven days ago.

Hello and welcome to live, minute-by-minute coverage of Sunderland v Arsenal at the Stadium of Light. Sunderland are the latest team tasked with stopping Arsenal, who have begun their title defence in formidable style: they’ve won out of three, including a dominant comeback victory against Chelsea last weekend, and look well equipped to become the first Arsenal team to retain the title since the mid-1930s.

There’s a long way to go, and Arsenal fans will remember how blisteringly they started their last two title defences in 2002-03 and 2004-05, only to ultimately fall short. But right now, they could barely be in better shape. Their fine start to the season came with a Champions League win in Naples, achieved despite a delay to their flight from London.

“I love those challenges,” noted Mikel Arteta. “I try to create them in pre-seasons so when they happen, we already experience them and we already know. So get to the stadium very late, change the routine and suddenly the players have to do something else.

It has been revealed that “Because when it happens, and it can happen, you can miss the flight, the train can be delayed, there’s so much traffic and I don’t want the players, but not only the players, the staff as well, panicking. So when that happens, adapt to it.”.

In a recent development, arteta has tested his squad in a variety of ways. “[We have] delayed the meals, delayed the transport, taken a different route. We’ve done many things – made the dressing room hotter, more difficult, more challenging, less beds... because we’re going to have to adapt to different contexts.”.

So far, they’re adapting very well to the context of being the reigning champions.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that il progetto per la trasformazione dell’area di San Siro torna al centro del confronto nel Comune di Milano.
  • A firmare questa nuova lettera, inviata in risposta alla comunicazione del sindaco del 13 novembre, sono stati Enrico Fedrighini, Alessandro Giungi, Angelo Turco, Michele Sacerdoti, Francesca Cucchiara, Tommaso Gorini e Marco Fumagalli.
  • Industry observers note that scrive poi C&F: "Alla lettera è allegato anche un documento dei medici epidemiologi Isde, elaborato dopo la risposta di Sala.

It has been revealed that il progetto per la trasformazione dell’area di San Siro torna al centro del confronto nel Comune di Milano. Lo scrive Calcio e Finanza (clicca qui per leggere l'articolo completo) che spiega che sette consiglieri comunali hanno inviato una nuova lettera al sindaco Giuseppe Sala, chiedendo di fermare la valutazione ambientale strategica (VAS) in corso e di integrarla con una valutazione di impatto sanitario (VIS).

A firmare questa nuova lettera, inviata in risposta alla comunicazione del sindaco del 13 novembre, sono stati Enrico Fedrighini, Alessandro Giungi, Angelo Turco, Michele Sacerdoti, Francesca Cucchiara, Tommaso Gorini e Marco Fumagalli. "Non mettiamo in dubbio il fatto che sia Lei che la giunta condividiate l’attenzione da noi espressa nei riguardi dell’impatto sulla salute dei nostri concittadini . Il tema centrale è che questa attenzione condivisa deve tradursi, per garantire il raggiungimento dell’obiettivo dichiarato, in conseguenti azioni e scelte concrete" la premessa dei consiglieri, riferendosi alla trasformazione dell’area, alla costruzione del nuovo stadio e alla parziale demolizione del Meazza.

Industry observers note that scrive poi C&F: "Alla lettera è allegato anche un documento dei medici epidemiologi Isde, elaborato dopo la risposta di Sala. I consiglieri lo citano a sostegno della necessità di considerare l’intera area interessata dalla pianificazione e di applicare un’analisi epidemiologica. Per i firmatari, la distinzione tra piano e singolo progetto richiamata dal sindaco conferma l’esigenza di 'adeguate metodologie di valutazione preventiva del rischio sanitario' sull’insieme della trasformazione prevista".

#15038. Breaking: Boston was a lovely holiday romance, but let's leave it there. Talk of taking Tartan Army back there every two years is just cringeworthy
