SCOTLAND 2 NORTH MACEDONIA 1: John McGinn at the double to spare the blushes of Pocognoli's shaky Scots on skipper Robertson's substantial night

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1540 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
  • Published: 17:01 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 17:11 EST, 13 November 2026.
  • On the night when the nation looked over its shoulder and celebrated the past, the here and now for Scotland looked distinctly uncertain.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 17:01 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 17:11 EST, 13 November 2026.

On the night when the nation looked over its shoulder and celebrated the past, the here and now for Scotland looked distinctly uncertain.

Coming 40 years and a day after his friend, Sir Kenny Dalglish, pulled on a Scotland jersey for the 102nd and final time, Andy Robertson joined the great man on a mark which, for years, seemed beyond the reach of mere mortals.

Industry observers note that by time up, history had mercifully repeated itself at Hampden. Back in the day, Dalglish, by then player-manager at Anfield, sailed into the international sunset on the back of a routine 3-0 win over Luxembourg.

Industry observers note that facing another opponent of modest ability, Robertson’s red letter day didn’t go quite as smoothly. Yet, when the Tottenham man is old and grey and reflecting on the night he created history, the annals will at least record a slender victory.

While his side did just about enough to prevail here, this was another fraught night for Sebastien Pocognoli.

You can talk about the need for patience under the latest manager until the cows come home. But North Macedonia are 71st in FIFA’s rankings. Scotland are 43rd.

John McGinn celebrates in trademark fashion after netting Scotland's winner from the spot.

At Hampden Park, in front of an expectant crowd, Scotland should be putting them to the sword with something to spare.

According to recent reports, yet, for long enough, the Belgian’s latest-look side were flat, predictable and plodding. It remarked much that it took the intervention of VAR for them to get the penalty which would ultimately lead to three points being accrued.

John McGinn’s second half double saved the Belgian’s blushes and truthfully there was little else to get the Tartan Army off their seats.

Too many big-name players scarcely merited pass marks. Too few looked comfortable in the system the manager is trying to bed in.

Recent findings suggest that if it was a step in the right direction, it was a small one. After five games under the affable Belgian, the progress has certainly not been startling.

While it goes without saying that beating the Swiss in St Gallen on Monday will be an inordinately tougher task, having some hope of moving up a place and securing a kinder draw for the Euros is still better than no hope.

Regardless of what pot they end up in when the draw is made in Belfast next month, a radical improvement will certainly be required across the board if they are to stand any chance of qualifying for the tournament via the front door.

As well as the achievements of Robertson and Dalglish, the career of Craig Gordon was acknowledged before the match with the 84-times capped keeper deservedly afforded a warm hand by the Tartan Army.

McGinn slots home his penalty after Ben Gannon-Doak had been brought down in the area.

Sources indicate that there were absolutely no excuses for Scotland here. North Macedonia were a tier-two team in name only. They arrived at Hampden having not won in 12 matches and not scored in eight.

Another Pocognoli game saw another back-three combination. This time Luke Graham was selected in the centre of the unit with Ryan Porteous and Kieran Tierney deployed either side of the Stoke man in what were their first appearances under the Belgian.

Robertson and Ben Gannon-Doak were tasked with providing the width in the 3-4-3. Scott McTominay slotted back into an advanced role beside John McGinn with the returning Che Adams asked to lead the line.

Industry observers note that for all there was a healthy crowd in excess of 40,000 inside Hampden, the atmosphere was subdued. In the four Nations League games to date under the fresh manager, the side hadn’t exactly given the supporters much to feed off.

In a recent development, despite some big guns returning, Scotland made a laboured start to their night’s work. It stated much that Graham, on his second appearance, was busier than any defender in white.

The first opening came as a result of an opposition error. John McGinn found Billy Gilmour who fed the overlapping Robertson. The skipper’s cross was well out of Adams’ reach.

Sebastien Pocognoli got his first Hampden win as Scotland boss but it was a nervy night.

It has been revealed that although Ljupche Doriev worried Angus Gunn with a curling effort, Scotland began to exert some degree of control on the match. Lewis Ferguson kept the visitors hemmed in with a header into McTominay’s feet. The Napoli man saw his shot on the spin well saved by Stole Dimitrievski.

Pocognoli was frustrated when Slovakian referee Michal Ocenas blew for a foul on McTominay, his justifiable gripe being that playing an advantage would have seen Robertson have a crack at goal.

Dimitrievski had a decent night. Although Adams’ flashing header from McGinn’s corner took a deflection, a reflex save at his near post added to Scotland’s frustration.

It has been revealed that north Macedonia were a spirited but ordinary side. They still had enough to thwart Pocognoli’s men.

Gannon-Doak saw plenty of the ball down the right, yet the end product often wasn’t there. The Bournemouth man did tee up Billy Gilmour for one dangerous cross. McTominay tried to replicate his iconic overhead kick against Denmark nearly a year ago. This time, his aim wasn’t true.

You could hardly blame Pocognoli’s star man for failing to find the net on that occasion.

Scott McTominay attempts an overhead spectacular a year on from THAT goal at Hampden.

According to recent reports, that wasn’t the case a few moments later when Adams slipped him in. Dimitrievski saved McTominay’s strike with an outstretched leg when he should have been picking the ball out of his net.

Adams had just blazed a strike high over the top while one-on-one with the keeper although the offside flag saved his blushes.

The visitors came closer to edging ahead when Eljif Elmas played the pass of the match over Scotland’s static defence to pick out Ezgjan Alioski. His lay-off was smashed into the side net by Enis Bardhi.

According to recent reports, A wholly uninspiring first-half concluded with Robertson advancing up the left and launching a cross halfway to Castlemilk. This was not going well.

Pocognoli waited on the edge of the pitch for his players returning, his enthusiastic applause clearly audible in the arena.

In a recent development, his hopes of a breakthrough at the outset of the second period were dashed in extraordinary fashion. Adams did well to chase a ball down to the line and cut it back. McTominay and his marker couldn’t connect, leaving Gilmour the simple task of firing into an unguarded net. Leaning back, his failure to even hit the target was unfathomable.

Elmin Rastoder celebrates after silencing Hampden with a leveller for North Macedonia.

Within seconds, the sense of relief inside Hampden was palpable as the opener finally arrived. Porteous got enough distance on his clearing header for Adams to barge Visar Musliu out of the way.

McGinn was alert to the situation and burst into the box. His crisp strike finally had the beating of the goalkeeper.

It should have settled Pocognoli’s side and paved the way for a comfortable result. Instead, they were pegged back within three minutes.

It was all just so simple and so avoidable. Bardhi’s whipped corner only needed McTominay to outjump his man. Flat-footed as the delivery arrived, he could only watch on in horror as Elmin Rastoder’s flashing header beat Angus Gunn.

Recent findings suggest that although Gilmour worked the keeper with a low strike, North Macedonia also sniffed a second goal. Time and time again, they got into pockets of space on the flanks and fired in dangerous crosses.

According to recent reports, adams made way for Oli McBurnie, the Hull man desperately hoping for his first goal on his 21st international appearance. He had a gilt-edged chance to get off the mark when rolled in by McGinn, but selflessly passed to the overlapping Gannon-Doak.

Scotland move on to their final game away in Switzerland as they look to finish on a high note.

Industry observers note that the winger appeared to take a heavy touch which allowed the keeper to rescue the situation. VAR, however, spotted that Dimitrievski had impeded him. Penalty.

McGinn did the necessary from 12 yards, smashing the ball straight down the middle for his 24th international goal.

North Macedonia, to their credit, kept going for it. They sensed a fragility in Scotland. Everyone in the ground could.

McGinn’s calm conversion proved to be just about enough to get the job done. But it’s fair to suggest that we are still awaiting lift-off in the latest era.

SCOTLAND (3-4-1-2): Gunn; Porteous, Graham, Tierney; Gannon-Doak (Hickey 76), Ferguson, Gilmour (Christie 76), Robertson; McGinn; Adams (McBurnie 67), McTominay. Booked: Ferguson. Manager: Sebastien Pocognoli.

Sources indicate that NORTH MACEDONIA (4-2-3-1): Dimitrievski; Ilievski, Mladenovski, Musliu, Alioski; Gashtarov (Elezi 64), Elmas (Stankovski 78); Churlinov (Maleski 64), Bardhi, Doriev (Nikolov 85); Rastoder. Booked: None. Manager: Goce Sedloski.

Referee: Michal Ocenas (Slovakia).

(ANSA) - MILANO, 16 NOV - "Chivu merita la Panchina d'oro per quello che sta facendo, quello che ha fatto e quello che farà". Javier Zanetti promuove il lavoro del tecnico nerazzurro, premiato a Coverciano con il riconoscimento riservato agli allenatori. "Sono felicissimo per Cristian - spiega il vice presidente dell'Inter, a margine del Trofeo Italo Galbiati -, lo conosco da quando eravamo compagni, è un fratello per me e non avevo dubbi su quello che poteva fare. Sta facendo un ottimo lavoro insieme a una squadra di ragazzi con grande personalità e responsabilità. È uno di famiglia, conosce i valori dell'Inter e sa trasmetterli ai giocatori".

Industry observers note that L'Inter, dopo i successi della scorsa stagione, non intende nascondere le proprie ambizioni. "Vogliamo essere competitivi in tutte le competizioni. Ci sono i presupposti per fare bene e sperare, ma non sarà semplice: sono tre competizioni difficili. Il campionato italiano è molto equilibrato e sarà una lotta fino alla fine". Il vicepresidente nerazzurro spende poi parole importanti per Lautaro Martinez: "Quando ci siamo conosciuti era molto giovane e aspettavamo questo suo presente. È un ragazzo di grande personalità, trasmette senso di appartenenza e ha sempre voglia di mettersi a disposizione per primo. Siamo contenti che sia il nostro capitano". Infine, una battuta su Nico Paz, accostato in passato all'Inter: "È un giocatore del Como e lo rispetto per questo". (ANSA).

Sources indicate that una tragedia ha colpito nelle ultime ore il calcio argentino. Abel Nunez, giovane calciatore dell'FC Ezeiza, è morto domenica 15 novembre in seguito alle conseguenze di una pallonata ricevuta alla testa durante una partita delle giovanili. Il ragazzo, classe 2008, era stato ricoverato e sottoposto a un intervento chirurgico, ma le sue condizioni non sono migliorate. I.

Industry observers note that L'episodio risale a giovedì 12 novembre, durante la partita tra FC Ezeiza e Deportivo Muñiz, valida per la sesta giornata della Copa de Plata del torneo Juveniles C organizzato dalla federazione argentina. L'incontro si disputava presso il centro sportivo del Club Atlético La Sonia, nella località di José C. Paz, nella provincia di Buenos Aires. Secondo la ricostruzione della stampa argentina, Núñez è stato colpito alla testa da un pallone calciato durante un rinvio ed è caduto a terra privo di sensi. Immediati i soccorsi e il trasferimento in ospedale, dove è stato operato. La partita è stata sospesa, così come quella della categoria successiva.

Recent findings suggest that oltre a giocare nelle giovanili dell'Ezeiza, Núñez faceva parte della squadra riserve di futsal del Nueva Estrella, club nel quale militava dal 2024. Quest'ultima società ha sospeso gli impegni sportivi previsti dopo la notizia della morte, compresa la partita con l'Argentinos Juniors. Anche l'FC Ezeiza ha pubblicato un lungo messaggio di cordoglio, ricordando il giovane compagno di squadra e rivolgendo le proprie condoglianze alla famiglia. Alla vicinanza espressa dai due club si è aggiunta quella della federcalcio argentina (AFA), attraverso il presidente Claudio Tapia, mentre numerose altre società hanno manifestato pubblicamente il proprio cordoglio.

Inside Boreham Wood, the only unbeaten team in England's top seven tiers: Boss LUKE GARRARD explains how play-off heartache and a 'genius' owner are fuelling his swashbuckling side's promotion bid

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 21:00 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 17:17 EST, 13 November 2026.
  • Of 252 clubs in the top seven tiers of English football, the last one unbeaten can be found in the pristine confines of Meadow Park, yards from the studios where the Indiana Jones adventures were filmed.
  • Recent findings suggest that boreham Wood are on their own crusade.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MATT BARLOW, FOOTBALL WRITER.

Published: 21:00 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 17:17 EST, 13 November 2026.

Of 252 clubs in the top seven tiers of English football, the last one unbeaten can be found in the pristine confines of Meadow Park, yards from the studios where the Indiana Jones adventures were filmed.

Recent findings suggest that boreham Wood are on their own crusade. And the Holy Grail is a long-coveted place in the EFL for the runaway leaders of the National League. They have 44 points from 16 games with 44 goals and are 12 points clear ahead of a trip to Yeovil on Saturday, finding success with a distinct passing style.

In a remarkable 4-3 comeback win against Hartlepool earlier this month, Luke Garrard's team made 1,022 passes, beating the Premier League record of 1,015 set by Manchester City against Swansea in April 2018.

The electric start to this campaign is, according to Garrard, fuelled by the lingering pain of defeat in the play-off final at Wembley in May when they conceded an equaliser in the seventh minute of stoppage time and lost on penalties.

'That broke me mentally for four or five days,' the Wood boss tells Daily Mail Sport. 'I reflected hugely and had a long, hard look at myself because I could not walk back for the first day of pre-season without the energy and heart for the job.

'I spoke to the owners and the staff about the first meeting I wanted to have when we came back in. It involved everyone at the club, and it was a message to tell all of them that as much as it hurt us, we needed to use the hurt as our fuel and our driving force.

'We got quite lucky getting some results on the board quite rapidly and that builds momentum and belief.'.

National League leaders Boreham Wood, under the guidance of their manager Luke Garrard, are the last unbeaten team in the top seven tiers of English football.

Boreham Wood are a slick operation, skilfully run despite crowds seldom breaking 1,500. They share Meadow Park with Arsenal Women and Arsenal Under 21s and U18s.

Industry observers note that boreham Wood are a slick operation, skilfully run despite crowds seldom breaking 1,500 by chairman Danny Hunter and his son Charlie, who is the sporting director and in charge of recruitment strategy. They are punching above their weight with a mid-table budget.

Hunter senior is a former props master in the film industry who worked at the nearby Elstree Studios among others, and whose father Mickey was a double promotion winning manager of club in the 1970s.

He took control in 1999 and has overseen investment of more than £14million and the rise from the depths of the Isthmian League to the brink of the EFL, forging effective relationships with local authorities and Premier League neighbours Arsenal, who use Meadow Park for their Women, Under-21 and Under-18 teams.

Arsenal ad boards surround an immaculate pitch, and work is underway at the venue on a £4m project to create a covered South Stand terrace incorporating improved 'Fan Zone' style facilities for away fans and a new first-team building.

Garrard's team train in the mornings on the artificial pitches beside the stadium, which are available for community use in the evenings and home in the afternoons to the club's academy.

In a recent development, manchester City's Iliman Ndiaye and Hull's Sorba Thomas were both nurtured as young players at Boreham Wood. So was Abdul Abdulmalik, a 23-year-old winger signed after his release from Millwall in 2024 and sold to Djurgardens in Sweden for £1.5m in August.

The Abdulmalik fee shattered the non-League record set when Fleetwood Town sold Jamie Vardy to Leicester in 2012.

Recent findings suggest that there was an untidy episode towards the end of the transfer window when Abdulmalik went public to plead for a move, but the Hunters secured an enviable price for their star and in another example of their good housekeeping have yet to reinvest the money in the team. It is still there as a war chest as they target promotion.

Abdul Abdulmalik, a 23-year-old winger signed after his release from Millwall in 2024, was sold to Djurgardens in Sweden for £1.5million in August.

Industry observers note that the club is run by chairman Danny Hunter (pictured) and his son Charlie, who is the sporting director. Hunter Snr is a former props master in the film industry.

The windfall from Wood's famous FA Cup run in 2021-22 was invested into refitting the interiors of the ground including the dressing rooms and swish hospitality areas recognised among the best in non-League.

Meadow Park has a bar bedecked with souvenirs from those games and named in honour of Mark Ricketts, scorer of the goal to beat Bournemouth, who were at the time bound for promotion to the Premier League, and which clinched a date with Everton in the fifth round at Goodison Park.

'At no stage has the chairman given me any pressure to generate money from prize funds and cup runs,' says 41-year-old Garrard. 'It's only ever been about creating moments and memories.

Sources indicate that 'He (Hunter) is a Boreham Wood boy through and through and it's always been his greatest wish to lead the club into the EFL. He wants to leave a legacy. I adore him, I think he's a genius. We have a great working relationship. I do not take for granted the luxury of being manager here, especially after losing my job two years ago.'.

Garrard has a long association with the club. First as a player, briefly in 2005 and then returning for a second spell four years later, a loan move from Wimbledon which became permanent and led him into his first coaching roles and the manager's job.

Sources indicate that he took control in 2015 with the Wood in the top tier of non-League for the first time. Three times they reached the play-offs without promotion and there were many highs including Goodison before Garrard's tearful exit after relegation in April 2024, only for him to be back in charge by September.

During five months away, he turned down interest from one club because it took him too far from his family home and received two direct and sobering rejections from National League clubs. Feedback from the first told him he 'wasn't on the list and never would be' and from the second that he 'wasn't good enough' for them.

Perhaps it reveals some of football's inherent petty-mindedness towards Boreham Wood. They are perceived by some as upstarts with limited history and small crowds, putting the noses of 'bigger' clubs out of joint with the streamlined success of their business model and Hunter's backing, like a non-League version of Bournemouth or Brentford.

Recent findings suggest that they have been known to charge scouts for tickets and charge away teams to broadcast, which some refuse to do on a point of principle. For a time, they had a reputation for pragmatic and unattractive football – but not any longer.

Garrard was rejected by two National League clubs and found himself back at Boreham Wood. 'The stars aligned,' as he puts it.

Prolific striker Matt Rush has is fuelling Boreham Wood's promotion push.

It has been revealed that garrard was probably entitled to have expected more interest in his services. Instead, he spent two days following the second of those rejections in earnest conversation with his wife about the need to look for work away from football when out of the blue came a call from Boreham Wood.

Within another two days he was back in his old job. 'The stars aligned,' as he puts it. 'It was the best team in the National South with the best players, the best facilities and the best budget. I had to go and deliver.'.

And he did. With promotion back to the National League at the first attempt. Then the near-miss heartache of Wembley. Now this early-season surge thanks in part to the goals of striker Matt Rush. The Wood seem to have emerged stronger despite selling their most talented individual, which is a reassuring situation for any coach.

Unbeaten since April in the National League, they scored 25 goals in seven games in October and League One Wigan became the first team to beat them in any competition this season, in the FA Cup first round on Saturday.

It could yet prove a blessing in Boreham Wood's quest for the Holy Grail.

Recent findings suggest that nella lista dei giocatori infortunati in casa Milan, il focus di questa sosta è stato su Pavlovic, Tomori e Loftus-Cheek, a cui si è aggiunto anche Mike Maignan dopo Francia-Turchia di domenica sera. La redazione di MilanNews.it fa il punto sulle condizioni dei quattro giocatori, mentre per Gabbia, Saelemaekers e Chukwueze se ne riparlerà nel 2027.

Industry observers note that per il portiere rossonero sono arrivate ottime notizie: l'esito degli esami di Mike Maignan svolti in data odierna è negativo, con il portiere francese che non ha nessun tipo di lesione. Nell'ultima partita con la Francia ha accusato un risentimento alla zona adduttoria, senza aver subito però danni o lesioni: il fastidio è in miglioramento. L'estremo difensore sarà a disposizione per Milan-Frosinone di domenica pomeriggio a San Siro.

According to recent reports, nella partita di Nations League tra Francia e Turchia Maignan aveva lasciato il campo all'intervallo per un problema agli adduttori nato da uno scontro di gioco con un avversario. Nella giornata di ieri L'Equipe aveva anticipato che i primi test medici avevano lasciato sereno il portiere, e gli esami svolti con lo staff medico rossonero che confermano le prime sensazioni: il portiere non ha riportato lesioni e sarà a disposizione per la sfida di San Siro contro il Frosinone.

It has been revealed that oggi visita di controllo per Fikayo Tomori e Loftus-Cheek per capire come precede il processo di guarigione dai rispettivi infortuni muscolari. Il più vicino al rientro è il difensore: il suo recupero procede bene, ha già ricominciato un lavoro individuale sul campo e dalla prossima settimana è previsto il suo ritorno graduale in gruppo. L'ex centrale del Chelsea sarà quindi costretto a saltare anche la sfida di domenica contro il Frosinone a San Siro.

It has been revealed that ci vorrà più tempo invece per rivedere in campo Loftus-Cheek che sta proseguendo il suo percorso di recupero nel rispetto delle tempistiche inizialmente previste. Tra circa due settimane, il centrocampista inglese si sottoporrà ad un nuovo controllo medico così da definire i successivi step del percorso verso il rientro in campo. Ovviamente non sarà a disposizione per Milan-Frosinone.

According to recent reports, oltre Maignan anche Strahinja Pavlovic punta il Frosinone con decisione: il difensore serbo oggi a Milanello ha svolto parzialmente l'allenamento in gruppo. Prosegue bene il recupero dopo che ieri aveva fatto solo del lavoro individuale. Il problema di coliche renali che gli ha fatto saltare la chiamata della Serbia sembra alle spalle: nei prossimi giorni è previsto il rientro totale in gruppo e il difensore centrale va verso il recupero per Milan-Frosinone di domenica 22 a San Siro dopo aver saltato le ultime due partite.

Il Corriere del Mezzogiorno si sofferma sulla chiusura del bilancio del Napoli che al 30 giugno 2026 ha realizzato un utile di 2,2 milioni in virtù del ritorno in Champions, definendo questo aspetto “una boccata d’ossigeno anche per il mercato di gennaio, tenendo conto dei parametri e della condizione dell’organico, con il rischio di non avere gli introiti della partecipazione alla Champions nella prossima stagione e senza plusvalenze di grande spessore da poter immaginare. Conquistare il passaggio ai play-off in Champions e risalire la classifica in campionato non sono solo obiettivi sportivi ma anche percorsi rilevanti sotto il profilo economico. Giocarsi dei traguardi che portano incassi significativi potrebbe spingere il Napoli ad anticipare le trasformazioni dell’organico che dovranno essere compiute in estate”.

In a recent development, after a humiliating defeat by Grimsby Town in their previous League Cup campaign, Manchester United found a different way to exit the competition this time around. The jeers heard at the full-time whistle after throwing away a two-goal lead pointed to more worrying times a year on from Blundell Park.

For the first time in half a century, United lost a game at Old Trafford having led 2-0, highlighting the defensive problems Michael Carrick needs to solve after turning results around last season.

“What the f---ing hell was that?” shouted the home fans, in a chant that may have been aimed at the referee but equally applied to United’s players, who led through Shea Lacey and Mason Mount’s early goals.

It has been revealed that brighton cut through Carrick’s defence several times before staging their comeback with goals from Charalampos Kostoulas, Pascal Gross and Maxim De Cuyper. Carrick and his analysts will rewatch the footage of all three goals in horror at how they conceded.

Kostoulas halves the deficit! 🔵Brighton score on the stroke of half-time. pic.twitter.com/bGjN1w6s6c.

“I totally understand the feelings of the supporters,” Carrick mentioned. “We have to accept it. I totally accept it. It’s on me ultimately: as a team what we look like, how we play and what results you get. I take that. I’ll take the praise, I’ll take the criticism and the upset.”.

Erik ten Hag used the domestic cups to taste success while struggling in the Premier League, but one of those opportunities is now lost to Carrick, who must be careful not to spiral from a poor start to the campaign into crisis. Sunday’s trip to Fulham before the international break now feels like a substantial game for United and Carrick.

“We’ve gone out of the cup and the feeling around the place feels bigger than that,” Carrick remarked. “I’ll be honest about that, that’s how it feels, but it doesn’t have to be like that. If we win football matches again, it can go in a different direction.

“We have a significant game on Sunday that we have to prepare for. We’re out of this competition and we have to go back to winning football matches.

Recent findings suggest that “It doesn’t feel good at the moment. It doesn’t feel good. We have to go back to winning football matches. We want to win and want to win promptly. The next game is Sunday. That’s all I’m thinking about right now.”.

At the start of the evening it seemed that the tie would be remembered for Lacey scoring on his first start for United, the first teenager to do so since Marcus Rashford. In the week when JJ Gabriel, one of United’s great academy talents, asked to leave the club, a different United teenager was kissing the badge when he found the net.

Gross took his chance when United carelessly played the ball out of defence again, with Diogo Dalot’s clearance mishit. Luka Vuskovic’s header went straight into the United penalty area, with their centre-backs failing to react swiftly enough.

Fabian Hürzeler’s side can be considered this season’s entertainers, with this comeback going with their seven-goal thriller against Chelsea, putting four past Aston Villa and five past Coventry at the weekend. Next for them in the League Cup is Manchester City or Norwich away, although they are unlikely to fear any opponents.

“We take it how it is. We want to go as far as possible but if you want to win something you have to win at the highest level,” Hürzeler mentioned. “We have to stay very, very humble and get an understanding why we are at the place we are and getting the basics right and the small margins right. It is so vital we stay humble and then we can grow into the game.”.

For Carrick, matches such as this can define a United manager’s reign if he cannot turn results around. The image of Ruben Amorim in the dugout at Grimsby was one of the lasting impressions of last season before Carrick was brought in to salvage the campaign.

“We can’t put ourselves in that position after being ahead in the game and the game finishing like it did,” he stated. “So we’ve got to react to it. We’ve got another game on Sunday, we’ve got to react to it.”.

Carrick will want to make a better fist of the cup competitions, but he could really use a win of any kind after taking just four points from United’s first four league games of the newly introduced season.

There were no flags on the Stretford End for the game against City, as fans voiced their opposition to what they view as a heavy-handed ticketing policy. The club states the measures are to stop ticket-touting but critics believe many innocent season-ticket holders are being caught in the crossfire and having their tickets revoked.

Discontent is never too far away given the continued presence of the Glazer family, and confidence is fragile regarding the club’s sporting direction under Sir Jim Ratcliffe and Ineos.

Eppure, a gennaio il club lariano potrebbe tornare sul mercato per acquistare un altro centravanti. Una necessità inattesa, legata soprattutto alle condizioni fisiche di Kean e a un calendario sempre più impegnativo, tra Serie A e Champions League.

Ne parliamo nel podcast di oggi di TuttoMercatoWeb.com, in compagnia di Ivan Cardia.

L'infortunio di Kean, alle prese con un problema alla tibia, ha ridotto le alternative a disposizione di Cesc Fabregas. Douvikas sta vivendo un ottimo momento, ma non può essere l'unica soluzione per un attacco chiamato ad affrontare numerosi impegni ravvicinati. Le alternative interne, da Nico Paz a Baturina, comporterebbero modifiche all'assetto tattico della squadra.

It has been revealed that quali saranno le mosse del Como nel mercato di gennaio? Tra i profili accostati ai lariani c'è anche Sergio Camello del Rayo Vallecano, ma non è ancora chiaro se la società deciderà di investire su un altro centravanti o cercare una soluzione temporanea. Molto dipenderà dai tempi di recupero di Kean e dalle valutazioni della dirigenza, chiamata a completare una rosa costruita per competere ad alti livelli senza compromettere gli equilibri raggiunti.

Recent findings suggest that if Andy Robertson’s first 101 caps for Scotland taught him anything, it’s that we have never been a nation to make life easy for ourselves. It’s in our DNA.

Why, therefore, would he have expected cap No102 to be any different?

This was meant to have been a celebration of one of Scotland’s greatest-ever servants on the night when he equalled Kenny Dalglish’s total appearances against the whipping boys of Nations League Group B1.

As the cliché goes, there’s no gimmes at this level. But that’s nonsense. This is exactly what Robertson’s special night should have been. A gimme.

In a recent development, the visitors hadn’t registered a goal yet in this campaign, never mind a point. They were rotten when Robertson and Co scored twice without reply in Skopje last month, and it was the same story for much of this forgettable contest.

The problem is that Scotland weren’t much better. In the first half, at least.

Andy Robertson joined Kenny Dalglish on 102 caps as Scotland saw off North Macedonia.

Thankfully, they got the job done after the break to ensure it would be a night Robertson will look back on fondly after all.

He’s earned that too, even if his own individual performance didn’t quite hit the heights of so many that have gone before. But nobody will remember that.

Perhaps he knackered himself by covering what must have been around 10km in a small-sided kickabout during the warm-up. He may not have the same turn of pace in his arsenal that he possessed when he first broke into the international fold as a fresh-faced teenager. But, in terms of intensity, the 32-year-old is still an animal, in the nicest possible way. He hassled and harried every one of his team-mates throughout the pre-game stuff, barking out all sorts of instructions along the way.

In many ways, he is still the same standard-bearer he’s always been. It was a shame he couldn’t quite lead the way when the serious stuff got started.

Operating on the left-hand side of a four-man midfield, the Spurs man – as he does as frequently as ever – bombed up and down the flank all night. However, his deliveries from several promising positions weren’t quite up to scratch.

In a recent development, A couple hit the first man. A couple cleared the upright. None caused any sort of alarm in the North Macedonian backline.

Robertson was his customary energetic self as he bombed up and down the left-hand side.

He was made to work harder than he would have liked at the other end too, as the visitors threatened to spoil the party on more than one occasion in the second 45.

In truth, he didn’t look particularly comfortable in Sebastien Pocognoli’s latest-look side. Then again, few did.

The Belgian will be given plenty of time to really put his stamp on this Scotland team, but there’s no two ways about it. The early signs are uninspiring to say the least.

By the end, people got sick of the attritional style employed by Steve Clarke. Pocognoli arrived with a reputation for going with a more enterprising approach.

Industry observers note that really? It’s fair to say, the wait to see it in action goes on.

Recent findings suggest that it’s not the time to panic. But you get the sense patience is already being stretched amongst some sections of the Tartan Army.

Recent findings suggest that they weren’t shy in airing their frustrations last night. Scott McTominay was on the receiving end of a few grumbles, as was Ben Gannon-Doak who once again did so much right until the all-crucial crucial last bit.

Yes, he may have won the winning penalty which John McGinn duly slotted away, but let’s be honest, there was more than a touch of good fortune about it.

The Scotland skipper leads his side out at Hampden on a night he will remember forever.

He should have burst the net when put clean through by Oli McBurnie long before keeper Stole Dimitrievski caught him near the byline.

The Bournemouth youngster is seen by many as undroppable, and there’s merit to that argument in that Pocognoli doesn’t have anyone else like him to call upon. However, he needs to improve the final part of his game to ensure he becomes Scotland’s main man in the years to come.

Had Scotland been a few goals to the good by the time McGinn stepped up to notch his second of the night, you suspect Robertson may have fancied taking the spot-kick himself.

If only it had been that comfortable.

Still, the record books will show that Robertson’s record-equalling night will ultimately go down as a triumph for all involved, even if it didn’t feel like it at the time.

La sfida è in programma il 22 dicembre alle 21 a San Siro; per i tagliandi sono previste prelazioni prima della vendita libera.

Recent findings suggest that la Supercoppa Italiana 2026 si giocherà il 22 dicembre a San Siro: l’Inter affronterà la Lazio alle 21, ora locale. Secondo quanto riportato da Goal, Per acquistare i biglietti, i canali indicati sono Vivaticket e i portali dei club, con fasi di prelazione prima dell’eventuale vendita libera. I prezzi riportati sono invece stime, non tariffe ufficiali.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

La competizione torna alla formula a due squadre e si disputa nuovamente in Italia. L’Inter partecipa da campione in carica della Serie A; la Lazio è la finalista sconfitta dell’ultima Coppa Italia.

I nerazzurri hanno preso parte alle ultime sei edizioni della Supercoppa, vincendo tre titoli consecutivi tra il 2021 e il 2023. L’ultimo successo biancoceleste risale al 2019. Lo scorso dicembre il trofeo è andato al Napoli, che ha battuto il Bologna 2-0 al King Saud University Stadium di Riad.

L’Inter di Cristian Chivu giocherà nel proprio stadio e arriva alla sfida con una serie di dieci partite senza sconfitte contro la Lazio. Tra queste, Goal indica anche il 2-0 nella finale di Coppa Italia di maggio.

I biglietti ufficiali per la Supercoppa sono venduti principalmente tramite Vivaticket, indicato come partner ufficiale della Serie A per la biglietteria, e attraverso i portali delle due società partecipanti.

Recent findings suggest that la vendita gestita dai club per le gare di Supercoppa segue solitamente più fasi. Si comincia, settimane prima della partita, con la prelazione per gli abbonati. Seguono le fasi riservate ai titolari della tessera del tifoso o della CRN; se rimangono posti disponibili, si passa alla vendita libera.

Per informazioni sui tagliandi, il riferimento indicato è costituito dai siti ufficiali dei club. La disponibilità sulle piattaforme di rivendita può essere consultata separatamente.

Goncalo Ramos is doing just about everything that can be asked of a centre-forward, except scoring goals regularly.

This morning’s Corriere dello Sport (via MilanNews) has a section headlined: ‘Now all Gonçalo needs is goals’. The Portuguese striker – who arrived at Milan in the summer for over €70m from PSG – has scored only three times so far in the league and Europa League.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Industry observers note that despite this, his involvement is constant and his stats speak for themselves. Ramos ranks second among strikers in Serie A in receptions, touches, and duels won, while he’s third in passes made. He ranks first in both interceptions and balls recovered, showing the spirit of sacrifice.

Expanding the discussion to forwards (so wingers included), Ramos is second in the league when it comes to total number of fouls committed and drawn with 41 in total, bettered only by Nicolo Cambiaghi of Bologna with 47.

Now, however, Ruben Amorim and the fans are expecting a breakthrough in scoring goals, which is what he was signed for and what is needed with a price tag so high. Only two have come from open play, and one of these was a gift from RB Salzburg.

A fresh striker will arrive in January who will have to alternate with the Portuguese. Fatigue could be one reason for Ramos being flat in front of goal given he has almost always started, as Francesco Camarda does not seem to have Amorim’s full faith yet.

È una sensazione agrodolce: abbiamo ottenuto la vittoria, ma non siamo riusciti a chiudere il girone tra le prime due. Nonostante questo, abbiamo dimostrato di potercela giocare contro chiunque. Dal punto di vista calcistico sto vivendo un ottimo momento alla Lazio. È una fase molto positiva per me, ma non ancora la migliore perché ho ancora tanto altro da dare.

Christian Zawieschitzky (02-05-2007), portiere austriaco del Red Bull Salisburgo di grandissime doti, cresciuto nella formazione austriaca mettendosi presto in luce, dopo aver fatto benissimo nelle giovanili, si è affermato al Liefering (club satellite del Salisburgo), e nell’estate del 2026 è tornato alla casa madre e in poco tempo si è preso il posto da titolare con grandissima sicurezza. Buonissimo senso della posizione, grande agilità, esplosività e fortissima personalità. Le nazionali austriache le frequenta sin dall’under 15 sempre con risultati lusinghieri. In questa stagione è titolare fisso della porta dei biancorossi sia in campionato sia in Europa League, e primeggia nelle classifiche individuali. Somiglianza: James Trafford (Leeds) Valore di mercato: 10 milioni €.

Industry observers note that idris Hopi (12-05-2008), esterno d’attacco ceco del Teplice. Veloce e tecnico esterno d’attacco di nazionalità ceca e di origini croate. Molto tecnico, ottima sensibilità di piede, bravo nel dribbling e nei tagli dall’esterno. Garantisce grande pericolosità e imprevedibilità al gioco d’attacco, sempre concentrato sul terreno di gioco, è considerato uno dei 2008 migliori del panorama calcistico dell’est Europa. Gioca in patria nel Teplice, club con cui è cresciuto e messo in mostra le sue tante qualità. La scorsa stagione con la formazione under 19 ha disputato un grande campionato e nella scorsa estate è salito in prima squadra imponendosi subito come titolare. Convocato in nazionale maggiore. Somiglianza: Jack Grealish (Everton) Valore di mercato: 2 milioni €.

In a recent development, wael Mohya (31-12-2008), trequartista/esterno d’attacco tedesco del Borussia Mönchengladbach. Origini marocchine per questo nuovo gioiello del calcio tedesco. Prodotto del Borussia Mönchengladbach, è dotato di grandissima tecnica di base, velocità di gambe e di pensiero, visione di gioco eccellente. Può essere impiegato sulla fascia o anche da trequartista vista l’inventiva, l’imprevedibilità e la grande capacità di assist. Marcatore più giovane in Bundesliga della storia del Borussia, in questa stagione (disgraziata) dei tedeschi sta risultando l’unica nota lieta del campionato, a conferma la convocazione in nazionale maggiore, dove Jurgen Klopp lo ha voluto per visionarlo da vicino e conoscerlo personalmente. Somiglianza: Marcus Tavernier (Bournemouth) Valore di mercato: 20 milioni €.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There was very much a Samba beat to this Manchester City victory – and it almost had a famous father in the crowd up dancing.

This was a night when Brazilian Allan Elias scored his first goal on an enterprising first appearance for City.

But it was another debutant who stole the show as the Carabao Cup holders sailed past Norwich City to set up a fourth-round meeting with Brighton.

Floyd Samba scored two fine goals and had a hand in another on a dream debut that had his beaming dad up off his seat and thrusting his arms in the air as if ready to party.

If the Samba surname feels familiar, that is because Floyd’s father Christopher played more than 200 games for Blackburn Rovers, Queens Park Rangers and Aston Villa.

In fact, it was very much a family affair as Floyd’s brothers Tyrone and Emerson, who are also in City’s academy and hoping one day to tread a similar path, joined in the jubilant celebrations alongside their mother, a visibly emotional Theresa.

Sources indicate that this particular evening belonged to Floyd, though. Deployed as a lone striker by Enzo Maresca, you would not have known he ordinarily plays as a midfielder such was the confidence and composure the 17-year-old oozed.

Norwich could not live with him or City for that matter as Maresca’s impressive start as manager since replacing Pep Guardiola continued apace.

Sources indicate that this must have been an incredibly satisfying moment for Samba Sr. He came through incredible hardship – at one stage as a teenager he was rough-sleeping – to forge an impressive career totalling more than 450 games for club and country.

So to be in a position to now have three sons in City’s academy and one produce a debut like this will fill him with enormous pride. Floyd was later seen enjoying a warm embrace with his dad in the crowd, moments after being congratulated by Tyrone, a year his senior, and 12-year-old Emerson, who plays for City’s Under-13s.

Sources indicate that “I knew there would be an opportunity to get some minutes for the first time with the first team – to get a debut like that is mind blowing,” Samba said. “I couldn’t believe it myself, but that’s just the beginning, I’ve got a significant career ahead of me. It was a great debut.”.

In a recent development, floyd caught the eye with a fine free-kick in City’s 2-1 FA Youth Cup final victory over Manchester United last season and now he has goals for the senior side to his name. Pretty stunning they were, too.

The first was a superbly steered header past two Norwich bodies on the line from Allan’s cross and the second a lovely, nonchalantly curled finish low into the far corner.

What a moment for Floyd Samba! 😍A goal on his Man City debut for the 17-year-old, son of former Blackburn defender Chris 🩵 pic.twitter.com/VCVfX9HCNn.

Chris Samba has deliberately kept a low profile, keen to let his sons get on with their own careers free of distractions, but there was no chance he was going to be able to suppress his emotions in that instant. And nor should he. It was some moment for the boy and his family.

According to recent reports, as impressed as Maresca was by the goals, it will have been other elements of Samba’s game that also caught the eye. He did extremely well to hold off the attentions of Norwich’s centre-backs when receiving a pass from Ayyoub Bouaddi and then returning the ball to the Moroccan who released Rayan Cherki through to score City’s second. His movement was also sharp, at one point taking a difficult pass sweetly in an adjusted strike, only for Norwich’s Bruno Alves to come across to make a timely intervention before Samba could get his shot off.

"Was there any doubt?"Ayyoub Bouaddi with his first assist for Man City as he sets up Rayan Cherki to make it 2-0 🔵 pic.twitter.com/0gfxp5GDXy.

Sources indicate that “It was satisfying not just for the two goals but for the entire performance,” Maresca said. “He didn’t play many games as a nine but he was good. He’s young, full of energy, strong, he can finish.”.

Allan, a £34m summer signing from Palmeiras, will have been just as pleased with his contribution. Maresca’s fluid formation initially resembled a 3-1-5-1 with Allan effectively operating as a right wing-back but he stuck doggedly to the task before eventually getting the moment to showcase his quality, first with his cross for Samba and later with a neat solo run and finish.

Driving inside Sam Field and then cutting back inside the Norwich man before curling an inch perfect finish into the bottom corner – all of it done with his left foot – it was quite the introduction.

Sources indicate that allan on his debut! 🇧🇷Magic from the Brazilian to make it 3-0 to Man City 💥 pic.twitter.com/nw6lNqh1yL.

Hugo Viana, City’s director of football, has said supporters will need to be patient with Allan and that it may take the 22-year-old time to adjust to English football but this first outing will do his confidence plenty of good.

“It was key for him to play 90 minutes and to see a little bit the English competition that is a bit different from South America so overall was good,” Maresca said.

Recent findings suggest that cherki was the only survivor from the team that started Sunday’s victory over Manchester United but it all felt pretty seamless from City. Bouaddi, the £85m signing from Lille, was poised and graceful in midfield alongside the impressive Mateo Kovacic and Geronimo Rulli could not have asked for a much quieter debut in goal.

Sources indicate that FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1.

Nico O’Reilly looked like he had barely broken a sweat despite Norwich’s players routinely being unable to keep up with him. Norwich themselves made nine changes but the gulf in class was enormous and testament to City’s strength in depth.

The game also gave Maresca the opportunity to give run outs to two more academy graduates who played in that Youth Cup final triumph, Kaden Braithwaite and Ryan McAidoo and the latter got his own name on the scoresheet to make it 5-0.

According to recent reports, all told there were seven City academy graduates on the pitch, two of them playing for Norwich. This was certainly a night to remember for the club’s youth production line.

Industry observers note that with the dominant performance, Man City have earned themselves the privilege of hosting Brighton in the next round, who will no doubt prove a much stiffer challenge than Norwich. They become the sixth all-Premier League tie in the next round, with only Fleetwood, Bradford and Peterborough remaining from outside the top flight:.

Possession: Man City 66% vs 34% Norwich.

Touches inside opposition box: 30 vs 4.

Industry observers note that erling Haaland left out of the squad, watching from the stands, would have enjoyed that performance from Floyd Samba. Here is his second goal for you to enjoy on his debut night:.

Five unanswered goals and a home-grown hero emerges for Manchester City!

It has been revealed that great through ball from O’Reilly, which Lewis lets run past him for the dummy. McAidoo runs on to it on the right of the box and first-time fires it low into the far corner.

It has been a perfect night for Manchester City’s academy.

Recent findings suggest that well we look like we’re heading for a matching scoreline to the previous edition of the fixture. That pesky shot on target is still eluding Norwich, whereas Samba is still out there looking for his hat-trick.

Two minutes of time to be added – who will get there first?

O’Reilly sends a high, looping ball to the back post from the left side, where McAidoo rushes to meet it but can’t get over it under pressure.

Final change for Norwich, as Kvistgaarden who has not had much service tonight, comes off for Schwartau.

The corner comes in to the centre of the box but is headed out by a City shirt.

It’s all slightly too little too late for Norwich.

They get another corner as Musaba tries to send a cross into the box from the right and it is blocked out.

Mo Touré strays just offside on the edge of the box, as Musaba sends a lovely little ball over to find him on the turn and the forward slots it past Rulli. Celebrations don’t quite begin before the flag goes up but that is a shame for the visitors.

Norwich have managed to get more of a grip in this half, despite conceding two more goals, but they are still without a shot on goal as we approach the final 15 minutes.

Another round of changes for both sides.

Man City take off scorer of their third goal Allan to bring on Braithwaite.

Norwich replace Ben Slimane and Bruno Alves with Touré and McConville.

Industry observers note that samba again at the heart of the action, laying off the ball to McAidoo on the right for the winger to run into the box. His shot towards the far post is saved low by Grimshaw who spills it almost into the path of Lewis, but Norwich survive.

Lewis makes a run down the right-hand side and crosses into Samba on the edge of the box. He lays off to McAidoo, but his shot goes sailing over the bar.

A surprise to no one, it is chucking it down in Manchester.

According to recent reports, substantial cheers from the away end as Norwich get their first corner of the evening. It is lofted high and long to the back post, where it is headed away by Bouaddi. It bounces out to Musaba, who has just come on, and he strikes it from the top of the box on the half-volley.

His shot cuts through a crowd in the box and has Rulli diving to his left, but it goes wide of the post. What an introduction that would have been!

Well all the stories from this match will be all about young Floyd Samba. Feel free to leave your best punny Samba/dance-related headlines in the comments section.

For Man City as you would expect it is all about game management from here on out.

Some more changes to report for Norwich as well, as Crnac is replaced by Musaba.

Wright is able to run in to space towards the edge of the box, but as has been their story all evening, his pass out to the wing is just not where it needs to be and their effort just breaks down.

What a way to score a second! A night to remember for Floyd Samba!

Norwich try and play out from the back but far too sloppy and Ait-Nouri picks up the ball on the left of the box. He has plenty of time to tee up Samba inside the box at the left corner, who finds himself with plenty of space to curl his shot into the far corner, beating the diving Grimshaw.

We may be seeing plenty more of him this season.

In a recent development, norwich looking for their way back into the game, as the ball comes down the left, fizzed in low and flashes past Rulli, trying to claim it. It deflects off a crowd of bodies and spins up, but Fisher can’t connect and it spins away harmlessly wide of the goal.

It is definitely Norwich’s best chance of the game and Fisher will be upset he hasn’t made more of that.

And Allan makes it three! Minutes after the restart, the Brazilian makes his own mark on his debut.

Maresca switched him onto the left side to escape Yongwa, and he picks up the ball outside the box and makes the run inside. He runs circles around Field and slots the ball home into the far bottom corner.

Some changes from both sides at half-time. McAidoo comes on for Cherki, though O’Reilly is the one to move up into midfield to fill the gap.

Norwich take off Diallo for Maghoma.

45 minutes left for the visitors to create something special!

Manchester City will be the ones to host Brighton in the next round – giving the visitors the opportunity to pull off a remarkable feat of knocking out both Manchester sides should they win.

A few minutes to remember here for Floyd Samba. First he steers home a very well taken header to give City the lead and then he plays a crucial role in the second, holding the ball up well before laying it off to Bouaddi to release Cherki to score. That’s how to make an impression on your debut.

Cherki is starting to get some momentum – but is swarmed by yellow shirts as he picks up the ball on the edge of the area.

Another loose ball from City in midfield and Norwich pick it up again. The ball to set the front line free is equally as loose from the visitors though and it breaks down once again.

Recent findings suggest that samba is looking lively, racing to get on a ball in front of Darling just on the edge of the box. Darling recovers to send it out for a corner, which becomes a free kick after Ait-Nouri wrestles his man to the ground at the back post as City are taking.

Wright sends a long ball across the field, looking for a man on the right side but Rulli is alert to it and comes to claim at the edge of the box.

Kovacic shows some promise with a strong run on the ball down the centre of the field, taking the ball all the way to the edge of the box, where he collides with a defender, and the ball spins away for Norwich to clear out.

This is better from City, who have looked like they’re lacking drive so far.

Yongwa again probing down the left side. It takes two to dispossess him and Man City manage to get the throw in, but approaching 20 minutes Norwich will be happy with this.

Kovacic loses the ball in midfield and Norwich surge forward. The move breaks down as Wright’s pass to Diallo on the wing is just behind him and he can’t take it forward into the box.

Sources indicate that spent the first 10 minutes trying to work out City’s system and settled on a 3-1-5-1, with Bouaddi operating as a nominal third centre-back, but it seems to have changed again now with O’Reilly dropping to left back and Bouaddi stepping into midfield. No doubt the metamorphosis will continue.

This Man City team have never played all together and it is clear that they’re still settling in here, figuring out how they’re going to press here.

Kovacic in the captain’s armband is tying it all together in midfield.

Khusanov threads a lovely ball to Samba who flicks it into the path of Lewis, who takes it and makes a run into the box. He creates space and sends a right-footed shot over the bar – but Man City are building.

Norwich make a move forward, with Yongwa bringing the ball down the left side but his cross into the box is blocked by Allan sliding in. The Brazilian is then fouled again as Yongwa tries to reclaim the ball and Man City get back in possession.

Sources indicate that it’s actually three Samba brothers at City. The youngest, Emerson, is also in the academy.

Early foul on Allan gets Man City a free kick and they have started as everyone expected they would – in plenty of possession.

They look for the early goal as O’Reilly feeds him in the from the left side, but the shot is blocked.

We have kicked off in Manchester!

With just over 10 minutes until kick-off here are the teams for tonight’s fixture:.

Man City XI: Rulli; O’Reilly, Vitor Reis, Khusanov, Lewis; Kovacic (c), Bouaddi; Ait-Nouri, Cherki, Allan; Samba.

Subs: Anderson, Braithwaite, Donnarumma, Fernández, Guéhi, McAidoo, Ndiaye, Matheus Nunes, Semenyo.

Norwich City XI: Grimshaw; Yongwa, Bruno Alves, Darling (c), Fisher; Field, Wright; Diallo, Ben Slimane, Crnac; Kvistgaarden.

Subs: Chrisene, Mattsson, Kovacevic, Maghoma, McConville, Musaba, Schwartau, Stacey, Touré.

As Abdukodir Khusanov makes his fourth start of the season, Hugo Viana, Man City director of football, has been speaking about the young Uzbek. The 22-year-old signed a newly introduced five-year contract with City in July, and Viana has affirmed that he “will be one of the best centre-backs in the world”.

"Abdukodir Khusanov will be one of the best centre-backs in the world" - Hugo Viana 🇺🇿🌏Full interview 🔗 https://t.co/dk3Qi8DF8D pic.twitter.com/hHdVdX5HSF.

It’s nine changes for Norwich from the squad that lost 4-3 to Middlesbrough on the weekend.

Norwich goalkeeper Daniel Grimshaw came through the ranks at Manchester City, joining as a teenager, so this will be a special night for the 28-year-old.

It has been revealed that speaking of Phil Foden, the winger will not be making an appearance tonight, as he is serving his three-match suspension following his sending off in the Manchester derby. The England international lashed out at Bruno Fernandes after the United captain had fouled him, resulting in a red card for violent conduct.

As well as this fixture, he will also be missing City’s game against Sunderland and the trip to Anfield to face Liverpool the following weekend.

We broke down the incident as it happened on Sunday and you can get the full story here.

Heavy squad rotation (10 changes in total for Maresca) has handed debuts for Gero Rulli in goal, as well as Allan and Floyd Samba in the outfield.

According to recent reports, 17-year-old Samba is the latest from City’s academy to be making his debut in the senior squad, following in the footsteps of Phil Foden, Rico Lewis, Nico O’Reilly and many more. A versatile midfielder, he has totalled 24 appearances across six competitions (incl Premier League 2) and scored 17 and assisted six goals in those matches.

Industry observers note that keep your eyes on young midfielder Floyd Samba, who has been handed his Manchester City debut tonight against Norwich by manager Enzo Maresca. Floyd is the 17 year old son of former Blackburn Rovers defender Christopher Samba.

In a recent development, his older brother Tyrone, 18, also plays for City. The siblings played in City’s FA Youth Cup final win over Manchester United last season, with Floyd scoring the first in a 2-1 win.

According to recent reports, city fans will also be keen to see how Allan Elias gets on on his first start, having arrived from Palmeiras for £34m. Geronimo Rulli also debuts in goal.

Good evening and welcome to another night of Carabao Cup coverage! It is the final fixture of round three (I promise) as Manchester City host Norwich.

Industry observers note that these two sides have not met since 2022, when Norwich were still in the top flight and were beaten 4-0 by City. Looking at their previous meetings, the odds are definitely stacked in favour of Enzo Maresca’s side, who have scored 14 unanswered goals in their last three meetings with Norwich, while the Championship side have not scored any.

City will be looking to make it six straight wins across all competitions tonight, having started perfectly in the Premier League with four wins from four, and comfortably seeing off Porto in their Champions League opener.

They were the talk of the weekend with their deeply controversial 1-0 win over rivals Manchester United as – having gone down to 10 men after Phil Foden was sent off – their winning goal was allowed to stand despite Enzo Fernández being clearly in an offside position that impacted United’s keeper and backline.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy.

City are defending their title in this competition – beating Arsenal last year in the final – but like all Premier League teams playing in European competitions, have only entered the tournament this year in the third round.

Philippe Clement’s side beat MK Dons 4-1 in the first round, and followed that up with a 2-1 win over Cardiff City in the second to reach the Etihad tonight. The fourth-round draw has already been done, and it has been decided that the winner of this match will face Brighton.

But we have at least 90 minutes of the third round left before that, so without further ado, we’ll get underway and bring you team updates shortly!

AC Milan must start thinking about the midfield of the future, and there are reportedly a few names on the list of ideas.

At 41 years of age Luka Modric, still remains simply irreplaceable for Ruben Amorim and for Milan. However, given that his deal expires at the end of the season, the Rossoneri management have a duty to also look to the future and prepare for the post-Modric era.

It has been revealed that the scouting team are very active in England, Spain, Belgium, and France, looking for the right players for Amorim’s footballing philosophy. Among the priorities for next season is identifying the right player to potentially take the reins as a deeper-lying playmaker.

Calciomercato.com report that three players have attracted considerable interest from Milan. One of them is Bournemouth’s Alex Scott, but he remains a dream at the moment because Arsenal and Chelsea have already swooped in on him.

The 23-year-old was called up to the England squad for the last break because manager Thomas Tuchel is very keen on him, but there’s a significant obstacle: the price tag. In England, there is even talk of a €100m+ asking price, given the clubs interested.

The spotlight has recently turned on Brighton’s Yasin Ayari too. He’s a highly versatile midfielder, performing at a high level both as a defensive midfielder and behind the striker. The Swede’s deal runs out in 2027 making him a major opportunity, but Brighton have a one-year option to.

Finally, we arrive at the latest name on the list: Adem Zorgane of Union-Saint Gilloise. Scouts like what they have seen from the Algerian, who combines physicality with good technical ability. He would likely be the cheapest of the three, but his potential is high in the eyes of Milan.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Il giudizio riguarda chi è rimasto a Roma durante la sosta; Agostinelli racconta anche di aver visto Frattesi sorridente.

Recent findings suggest that la Lazio non ha staccato la spina durante la sosta: è questo l’aspetto che ha più colpito il protagonista dell’intervento riportato da Radiosei e che gli dà sicurezza per il futuro. A suo giudizio, i giocatori rimasti a Roma hanno mostrato di voler restare concentrati e di meritare spazio. Nel suo intervento ha parlato anche degli infortuni, di Frattesi e della sua conoscenza con Kurt Baldacchino.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

L’intervento si apre con una precisazione: «Premesso che la mia conoscenza con Kurt (Baldacchino, ndr) risale a tre anni fa.».

In a recent development, lui è il presidente del ‘Lazio club Malta’ e appunto tre anni fa mi premiò quando allenavo l’altra squadra di Malta (il Gudja United Club). Quest’anno si divide tra la mia squadra, il Mġarr United, e le giovanili. Sapevo di questa cosa e pensavo si potesse risolvere. Quando siamo arrivati, io sono andato a casa mia a Roma e con la squadra e ci siamo rivisti direttamente a Formello, incontro Kurt, bravo ragazzo e tifosissimo della Lazio, e mi dice che era rimasto fuori. Eravamo però a ridosso della gara, quindi ho raggiunto la squadra. Speravo la situazione si potesse risolvere poi invece non è andata così e mi è molto dispiaciuto perché pensavo potesse essere un ‘giorno di festa’. Ad ogni modo è un ragazzo splendido, ognuno può esprimere le sue idee non gli darei ‘la croce addosso’. Probabilmente il fatto si poteva risolvere in maniera serena.

Gli infortuni della Lazio? Avendo degli staff molto numerosi ci sono confronti continui. Oggi lo staff è molto importante. Frattesi l’ho visto sorridente. Per me un giocatore può fare mille cose atletiche ma lo giudico ‘guarito’ se fa una partita, anche solo di 15′ perché non sei frenato durante la partitella. Questo però non significa che non ci saranno rischi in gara.

Recent findings suggest that di questa Lazio l’aspetto che mi ha impressionato, e che mi dà sicurezza per il futuro, è che non hanno staccato la spina. Questo non è importante, di più. Significa che chi era a Roma durante la sosta ha voluto dimostrare di stare sul pezzo, di meritare spazio”.

Scegli FcInter1908 come tuo sito preferito su Google: clicca qui.

È pronta a decollare la Nazionale Under 18, partita alla volta del Qatar, dove dal 19 novembre al 13 dicembre andrà in scena il Mondiale Under 17.

Per l’Italia si tratta dell’ottava partecipazione in 19 edizioni, mentre il miglior piazzamento è arrivato nella scorsa edizione, sempre a Doha, quando la formazione di Massimiliano Favo – attuale tecnico dell’Under 19 azzurra, impegnata nel secondo turno delle qualificazioni europee nelle Marche – conquistò una storica medaglia di bronzo battendo il Brasile ai rigori (Brasile-Italia 0-0, 2-4 dtr, 27 novembre 2025).

Il tecnico Daniele Franceschini ha convocato per l’occasione 21 calciatori, tutti nati nel 2009, fatta eccezione per il centrocampista dell’Atalanta Francesco Olivieri e per l’attaccante della Fiorentina Federico Croci, entrambi classe 2010.

It has been revealed that L’Italia, che si presenta all’Aspire Zone da campione d’Europa, è stata inserita nel Gruppo E insieme a Giamaica, Costa d’Avorio e Uzbekistan. L’esordio nella rassegna iridata è in programma venerdì 20 novembre (ore 16), sul Campo 3, contro i giamaicani. Lunedì 23 novembre (ore 15.30), nuovamente sul terreno di gioco numero 3, sarà la volta della sfida contro gli ivoriani, mentre giovedì 26 novembre (ore 15) la fase a gironi azzurra si chiuderà con il match sul Campo 5 contro gli uzbeki.

Portieri: 1 Lorenzo Costoli (Genoa), 18 Carlo Galliera (Inter), 12 Christian Lupo (Lecce);.

Difensori: 3 Matteo Albini (Como), 2 Giampaolo Bonifazi (Roma), 13 Jacopo Del Fabro (Juventus), 4 Djibril Diallo (Parma), 6 Andrea Donato (Inter), 14 Davide Rigo (Juventus), 5 Ludovico Varali (Parma);.

Centrocampisti: 16 Riccardo Cassano (Como), 8 Francesco Gasparello (Atalanta), 20 Gioele Giammattei (Roma), 15 Gianluca Tommaso Okon-Engstler (Club Brugge), 17 Francesco Olivieri (Atalanta);.

Attaccanti: 19 Tommaso Casagrande (Hellas Verona), 10 Thomas Corigliano (Juventus), 21 Federico Croci (Fiorentina), 11 Marcello Fugazzola (Atalanta), 7 Jacopo Landi (Lazio), 9 Diego Perillo (Atalanta).

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Prima di affidare la panchina a Mauricio Pochettino, il Manchester United avrebbe valutato diversi allenatori per sostituire Michael Carrick.

  • It has been revealed that tra le alternative valutate figuravano anche Antonio Conte, Eddie Howe e Julian Nagelsmann.

Prima di affidare la panchina a Mauricio Pochettino, il Manchester United avrebbe valutato diversi allenatori per sostituire Michael Carrick. Tra i nomi sondati dalla dirigenza ci sarebbe stato anche Didier Deschamps, ex commissario tecnico della Francia.

Secondo talkSPORT, i Red Devils avrebbero avviato alcuni contatti con Deschamps, senza però arrivare a una trattativa concreta. Lo United avrebbe anche sospettato che il tecnico stesse utilizzando l'interesse inglese per rafforzare la propria posizione nelle trattative con altri club. Sul francese, infatti, ci sarebbe stata un'offerta importante dell'Al Ahli: circa 25 milioni di sterline per tre anni.

Arsenal star Max Dowman smashes Jude Bellingham's record - but a less-familiar name should catch Thomas Tuchel's eye ahead of Euro 2028: THINGS WE LEARNED from England U21's defeat to Portugal

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1191 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 16:46 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 18:41 EST, 13 November 2026.
  • Max Dowman smashed Jude Bellingham's record on an icy cold night in Bristol to become the youngest player to ever play for England's Under-21s.
  • The 16-year-old was sent on with 30 minutes to go by Lee Carsley in a move that energised an Ashton Gate crowd that went home frustrated after a 1-0 defeat inflicted by Afonso Moreira's first half goal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 16:46 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 18:41 EST, 13 November 2026.

Max Dowman smashed Jude Bellingham's record on an icy cold night in Bristol to become the youngest player to ever play for England's Under-21s.

The 16-year-old was sent on with 30 minutes to go by Lee Carsley in a move that energised an Ashton Gate crowd that went home frustrated after a 1-0 defeat inflicted by Afonso Moreira's first half goal.

According to recent reports, but this was to be Dowman's night, smashing the previous record set by Bellingham when he made his England Under-21 debut against Kosovo in 2020 aged 17 years, two months and six days old. Dowman does not turn 17 until December 31.

Under-21s boss Lee Carsley has been keen long before this international break to try to shield Dowman from the weight of expectation.

But on he came, replacing the lively Amario Cozier-Duberry with a smile on his face and a quiet confidence that he didn't take long to show off, bursting past two Portuguese markers before four huddled together to gang up on him.

Breaking records is nothing latest to a player that already holds one for being the Premier League's youngest-ever goalscorer, thanks to his goal against Everton last season.

Max Dowman wrote his name into the record books once more, playing for England Under-21s.

Dowman came on to rich applause on a cold night in Bristol to shatter Jude Bellingham's record.

The Arsenal teenager was lively playing off the right as he now targets the 2027 U21 Euros.

Dowman is both the youngest player to ever win the Premier League and his outing in the Champions League against Slavia Prague last season saw the then-15-year-old become the youngest-ever player to appear in that competition.

By the time next summer's European Championships, which England will attempt to win for a third successive time, rolls around, rising star Dowman could well have earned the right to be this team's main man.

'We've only got three games left before the Euros [next summer],' Carsley explained.

'So it's crucial that he puts himself in the shop window to be on the plane.

'It's notable that he keeps playing well, getting minutes, showing a really good attitude, like he has done.

It has been revealed that 'I thought he was outstanding when he came on tonight. I thought all of the subs made a real impact.

'I thought Max was unlucky not to get an assist... he made a great pass to Mikey Moore.

'He took up some really good positions, both in the 10 and out wide, he's got a big future ahead.'.

His immense talent was one reason why Arsenal sent Ethan Nwaneri, who Dowman played alongside for part of his cameo, to Marseille on loan, and then similarly to Borussia Dortmund, eager not to block the 16-year-old's pathway.

Carsley knows the diamond he has on his hands and will want to take great care in helping polish a player that this crowd, this England team and this management group know has genuine world class potential.

Recent findings suggest that speaking of Nwaneri, this felt like a substantial camp for him. A big camp in the sense that he's falling down the pecking order at Dortmund and is back with a manager that has been so vital in his development.

Nwaneri was part of that 2025 group that won the Euros in front of Thomas Tuchel and he'll have seen the likes of Elliot Anderson and Alex Scott kick on to get to the seniors.

As previously mentioned, Nwaneri was moved out of the way by Arsenal to aid Dowman's development, not an easy pill for a player as talented as he is to stomach when his own development journey is at such a critical juncture given he is, to the surprise of many, still only 19.

'I think we have to remember his age as well,' Carsley added when asked about Nwaneri by Daily Mail Sport.

'He's very young is Ethan and he's another one that we've got a lot of hope for. He's got a lot of potential.'.

Ethan Nwaneri was pushed to the side at Arsenal to benefit Dowman but England is different.

Lee Carsley has been a crucial figure in the development of Nwaneri and this camp was timely.

It was telling that even when Dowman came on, even with the groundswell of excitement at his introduction, it was Carsley's call to keep Nwaneri in his preferred No 10 position with Dowman slotting in on the right.

Nwaneri has only started four games on loan at Dortmund this season and has not managed a single start in the Champions League.

His close control, his quick burst over five yards and the fluidity of his movement was a timely reminder that yes, Dowman is the rising star everyone came out to see, but Nwaneri won't get pushed to the side again without a fight.

Amario Cozier-Duberry is a name not all will be familiar with but come next summer, with the Euros in his sights and promotion to the Premier League on the agenda with Middlesbrough, that could all be about to change.

The 21-year-old has had to be very patient, waiting until last month to make his debut at this level after years of finding himself overlooked.

Here, in what was just his third Under-21 appearance, he showed over the course of 61 minutes why the days of being looked past should be over.

Industry observers note that one of the big frustrations in the FA right now at Under-21 level is the lack of touchline wingers. Rio Ngumoha, still only 18, has never been capped at the level and has instead been catapulted into the first team, while many, like Ethan Nwaneri, prefer playing inside.

'The more we can get our wide players one v one the better,' Carsley said. 'I think sometimes we leave them isolated and the opposition are able to double up on them.

Amario Cozier-Duberry is not a household name at international level but his talent is immense.

'It's crucial that our game blueprint can't just be to get the ball wide and hope for the best.'.

Dowman, on in place of Cozier-Duberry is a 10, rather than a right winger which is where he came on, and so a player like Cozier-Duberry, who is on loan at Middlesbrough from Brighton & Hove Albion, is worth his weight in gold.

Here in Bristol he was routinely drawing two defenders and at times three; Portugal knew full well how a quick flip-flap of the ball, or one clipped pass over the top, was enough for the Englishman to take the top off the back-line.

His loan at Bolton Wanderers last season complicated an international journey that has seen him play at Under-16, Under-17, Under-18, Under-19 and Under-20 level, but that's all in the past.

It has been revealed that england need a genuine, pacy threat out wide if they are to win a third straight Euros. Cozier-Duberry demonstrated here exactly why he should be it.
